title: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students (PMS-SC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice & Empowerment)
text: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students (also known as PMS-SC; other names: SC Post Matric Scholarship; Post Matric Scholarship SC; PMS SC) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (all States/UTs). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice & Empowerment). Implementing agency: State Governments/UT Administrations through National Scholarship Portal (NSP); funds released by Centre to States. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: 1944 (pre-independence scheme, revised many times). Operational period: Continuous; major revivals FY 2016-17, 2017-18, 2019-20 and 2024-25 onward. Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Pre-independence post-matric scholarship for Scheduled Castes; guidelines revised 2016, 2019 and 2024. Target group: Scheduled Caste students studying after Class 10 (Class 11 to PhD, including professional, technical and vocational courses). Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: No specific age limit. Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 2,50,000 from all sources. Eligibility: Student must belong to a Scheduled Caste; must be enrolled in a recognised post-matriculation course (Class 11/12, ITI, polytechnic, diploma, UG, PG, professional degree) in a government-recognised institution in India; scholarship is payable only for the prescribed duration of the course; student must not hold any other centrally funded scholarship for the same period Not eligible / conditions: Students who fail to promote to the next class lose the scholarship; only two members of a family can get this (and other such) scholarships simultaneously; distance/correspondence courses allowed only if the institution is recognised and there is no regular course available; income certificate and caste certificate from competent authority are mandatory Benefits: Reimbursement of all compulsory non-refundable fees (tuition, admission, exam, etc.) charged by the institution plus a monthly maintenance allowance. Also covers study tour charges (up to Rs 1,600 p.a.), thesis typing/printing (up to Rs 1,600 for PhD), book grant, and coaching for competitive exams for courses of less than one year; paid by DBT into Aadhaar-linked bank account Benefit type: Scholarship; Fee reimbursement; Education. Headline benefit value: Maintenance allowance (per month): Group-1 courses (Medicine/Engineering/Agriculture degree, MBA/MCA/LLB) hosteller Rs 1,200 (day scholar Rs 550); Group-2 (Pharmacy, Nursing, B.Ed., Mass Comm., etc.) hosteller Rs 820 (day scholar Rs 530); Group-3 (BA/BSc/BCom general, BBA, BCA) hosteller Rs 570 (day scholar Rs 300); Group-4 (Class 11-12, ITI, polytechnic, vocational) hosteller Rs 380 (day scholar Rs 230). Full compulsory fees paid. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 Centre:State for most States; 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States (100% central for UTs without legislature). Interest rate: Not applicable - scholarship. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Largest SC scholarship scheme - about 60 lakh SC students covered per year; over Rs 20,000 crore disbursed in the last decade. How to apply: Online only through the National Scholarship Portal (state schemes may also run on state portals) via National Scholarship Portal - scholarships.gov.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate from competent authority; income certificate (family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh); Class 10/previous exam marksheet; Aadhaar; Aadhaar-seeded bank account in student's name; admission/fee receipt; bonafide certificate; institute verification; passport-size photo. Helpline/contact: NSP helpline 0120-6619540 (helpdesk@nsp.gov.in); State social welfare/welfare department helplines. Key features: Oldest and biggest SC education scheme; covers full course fee plus stipend; 100% DBT; applies from Class 11 up to PhD; also gives coaching fees for short courses; renewed every academic year Recent updates: Income ceiling raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2.5 lakh (2019); maintenance rates revised upward; Aadhaar payment-bridge mandatory; Ministry has pressed States to clear arrears of scholarship dues to institutions since 2024-25 Sources: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment - Scheme list | https://socialjustice.gov.in/schemes | National Scholarship Portal | https://scholarships.gov.in | PIB / Department of Social Justice annual report content on PMS-SC.

title: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students studying in Classes IX and X (Pre-Matric SC (IX-X))
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students studying in Classes IX and X (also known as Pre-Matric SC (IX-X); other names: SC Pre Matric Scholarship; Pre-matric scholarship Class 9 10 SC) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (all States/UTs). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: States/UTs through National Scholarship Portal. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: Post-independence central scheme; current design from 2012-13, rates revised in 2019-20. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC students studying in Class IX and X. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines. Income limit: Parental/guardian annual income up to Rs 2,50,000. Eligibility: SC student studying in government, government-aided or recognised private school in Class 9 or 10; must appear for the prescribed annual examination; attendance and promotion norms apply Not eligible / conditions: Not for students in other classes; can be combined with other scholarships subject to ceiling rules; requires income certificate Benefits: Monthly scholarship to reduce drop-out between upper primary and secondary stage and to help SC students reach the post-matric stage, credited by DBT Benefit type: Scholarship; Education. Headline benefit value: Day scholars Rs 225 per month and hostellers Rs 525 per month (for 10 months in a year) as per revised central norms; some States top up the amount. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Over 40 lakh SC students annually (Central + State share). How to apply: Online through National Scholarship Portal; school verification compulsory via scholarships.gov.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account of student; admission proof; class promotion certificate; photo. Helpline/contact: NSP helpline 0120-6619540. Key features: Covers only Classes 9 and 10; paid for 10 months a year; hostellers get more than day scholars; delivered entirely by DBT Recent updates: Rate revision 2019 (day scholar Rs 225, hosteller Rs 525); income ceiling Rs 2.5 lakh; States advised to pay in one or two instalments per year Sources: Department of Social Justice & Empowerment - Pre-Matric Scholarship guidelines | https://socialjustice.gov.in | National Scholarship Portal | https://scholarships.gov.in.

title: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Children of those engaged in occupations involving cleaning and prone to health hazards (Pre-Matric (Unclean Occupations))
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Children of those engaged in occupations involving cleaning and prone to health hazards (also known as Pre-Matric (Unclean Occupations); other names: Pre-matric scholarship children of manual scavengers; unclean occupation scholarship) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: States/UTs through National Scholarship Portal. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: Long-running scheme; revised guidelines from 2012-13 and revised rates 2019-20. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: Children of persons engaged in unclean/health-hazardous occupations notified under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (tanners, flayers, waste pickers, sewer and septic tank cleaners, etc.) - open to all castes/religions. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Students of Classes I to X. Income limit: No income limit (occupation-based eligibility). Eligibility: Parent/guardian must be engaged in a notified unclean occupation as per the 2013 Act; child studying in Class I to X in a recognised school; application with occupation certificate Not eligible / conditions: Not applicable to children whose parents are not in the notified occupations; cannot draw two scholarships of the same nature Benefits: Monthly scholarship for Classes I-X plus ad-hoc grant for books, uniforms and stationery to enable children of sanitation workers to complete school Benefit type: Scholarship; Education. Headline benefit value: Approximately Rs 110-700 per month depending on class and day-scholar/hosteller status, plus an ad-hoc annual grant (about Rs 750-1,250) for books and stationery; amounts revised periodically - confirm current rates on NSP. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 (90:10 NE and Himalayan States). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Lakhs of children of sanitation workers/sweepers annually. How to apply: Online through National Scholarship Portal via scholarships.gov.in. Documents needed: Occupation certificate of parent/guardian (from local body); Aadhaar; bank account; admission proof; school certificate; photo. Helpline/contact: NSP helpline 0120-6619540. Key features: No income ceiling - eligibility is by parent's occupation; covers Classes I to X (unlike the general SC pre-matric scheme which covers only IX-X); intended to break inter-generational manual scavenging Recent updates: Occupations list aligned with the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act 2013; NAMASTE (2022) now also supports such families Sources: Social Justice & Empowerment - Pre-Matric Scholarship (cleaning occupations) | https://socialjustice.gov.in | National Scholarship Portal | https://scholarships.gov.in.

title: Central Sector Scheme of Top Class Education for Scheduled Caste Students (TCES-SC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Central Sector Scheme of Top Class Education for Scheduled Caste Students (also known as TCES-SC; other names: Top Class Education SC; Top Class Scholarship SC) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: Ministry's Top Class Education Cell / directly to institutions and students. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (100% central funding). Launched: 2007-08 (revised guidelines 2021 and after). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: Meritorious SC students admitted to premier Indian institutes (IITs, IIMs, NITs, AIIMS, NLUs, IISERs and other institutions identified by the Ministry). Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines. Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 8,00,000 (earlier Rs 6,00,000). Eligibility: SC student who secured admission to a notified premier institute for a full-time prescribed degree/diploma course; must not have availed any other scholarship for the same purpose Not eligible / conditions: Only notified institutes and courses are covered; benefits are not available for correspondence/distance courses Benefits: Full tuition and non-refundable fees, living expenses for the entire course duration, plus annual book grant and one-time computer purchase assistance Benefit type: Scholarship; Fee reimbursement; Education. Headline benefit value: Full tuition/non-refundable fees; living allowance about Rs 2,220 per month for hostellers (about Rs 1,110 per month for day scholars); book/stationery grant about Rs 3,000 per year; one-time computer purchase assistance about Rs 45,000 - confirm current rates with the Ministry/institute. Funding pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Scheme). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 1,000 fresh SC students every year (1,250 in some years) in about 265 identified premier institutes. How to apply: Online application to the Ministry's portal/institute nodal officer after admission; institute certification via scholarships.gov.in (NSP) / Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Top Class Education portal. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate; admission letter of premier institute; fee receipt; Aadhaar and bank details; Class 12 marksheet; institute endorsement. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, New Delhi. Key features: Covers boarding and lodging along with tuition at top institutes; separate from the mass Post-Matric scheme; supports SC students at IIT/IIM/AIIMS level Recent updates: Income ceiling raised to Rs 8 lakh; institute list expanded; payments routed through the institute to avoid delays Sources: Social Justice & Empowerment - Top Class Education for SC | https://socialjustice.gov.in | NSP scheme listing | https://scholarships.gov.in.

title: National Overseas Scholarship for Scheduled Castes, DNTs and landless agricultural labourers/traditional artisans (NOS-SC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: National Overseas Scholarship for Scheduled Castes, DNTs and landless agricultural labourers/traditional artisans (also known as NOS-SC; other names: National Overseas Scholarship SC; overseas scholarship for SC students) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment with Indian missions abroad. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 1954 as overseas scholarship for SC (present design from 2000s; guidelines revised 2019 and later). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC and DNT students and students from families of landless agricultural labourers and traditional artisans. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Below 35 years (and below 40 years for PhD). Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 8,00,000. Eligibility: At least 60% marks in the qualifying degree; admission to a Master's/PhD/post-doctoral course in a university abroad (QS top-500 universities prioritised); must give an undertaking to return to India after course completion Not eligible / conditions: Only one child per family can get the award; the award is not for undergraduate courses; scholars must return to India within 30 days of completing the course Benefits: Full tuition fees, annual maintenance allowance, airfare, visa fees, medical insurance and contingency grant for study abroad Benefit type: Scholarship; Education. Headline benefit value: 125 awards per year (115 SC, 6 DNT, 4 landless agricultural labourers/traditional artisans); 30% of slots reserved for women; maintenance allowance USD 15,400 per year (GBP 9,900 per year for UK) plus full tuition and other grants - confirm current currency rates and ceilings. Funding pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Scheme). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: 125 new scholars every year. How to apply: Online application on the dedicated NOS portal via nosmsje.gov.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate from Revenue Officer (not below Tehsildar); degree marksheets; unconditional admission offer letter; valid language-test score; passport; bank details. Helpline/contact: Overseas Scholarship Cell, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, New Delhi. Key features: Highly competitive, fully funded foreign education scholarship exclusively for SC/DNT candidates; 30% slots for women; covers top-500 QS universities; includes return-and-serve expectation Recent updates: Selection cycle opened for 2025-26 with 125 slots; provisional selection lists published on the portal; majority of awards now to STEM and professional courses Sources: National Overseas Scholarship portal | https://nosmsje.gov.in | Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (with UGC as implementing agency)
text: National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (also known as NFSC; other names: National Fellowship for SC; Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship SC (old name)) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (with UGC as implementing agency). Implementing agency: University Grants Commission (UGC). Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 2005-06 as Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship; renamed and revamped in 2012-13 and again 2019-20. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for SC Students (2005-06). Target group: SC students pursuing MPhil/PhD in Indian universities and institutions. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: As per UGC norms for MPhil/PhD admission. Income limit: No income limit, but the candidate should not be employed/ receiving other fellowship during the course. Eligibility: SC candidates who have registered for MPhil/PhD in a UGC-recognised university/institution; selection on the basis of merit in the qualifying Post-Graduate degree Not eligible / conditions: Candidates already receiving another fellowship or salary are not eligible for the same period; fellowship lapses on failure to submit progress reports Benefits: Monthly fellowship for MPhil (limited period) and PhD (full duration), plus HRA/hostel allowance and contingency/annual grant for research expenses; DBT-based Benefit type: Fellowship; Education; Research. Headline benefit value: Fellowship as per UGC rates (about Rs 37,000 per month in the initial two years as JRF and about Rs 42,000 per month thereafter for PhD) plus HRA and contingency grant of about Rs 12,000-25,000 per year; about 2,000 fellowships offered per year for SC students. Funding pattern: 100% Central. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 2,000 new SC fellowships per year; thousands of ongoing fellows. How to apply: Online through the National Fellowship portal (UGC/Social Justice & Empowerment) via nfsc.gov.in / scholarships.gov.in / UGC portal. Documents needed: Caste certificate; PG degree marksheet; PhD/MPhil registration proof; bank details; undertaking; guide/university endorsement. Helpline/contact: UGC helpdesk; Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment fellowship desk. Key features: Merit-based research fellowship for SC students; supports full PhD duration; paid directly to scholar's bank account; aims to increase SC representation in teaching and research Recent updates: Fellowship rates revised in line with UGC revision; slots increased to about 2,000 per year; digital onboarding through DBT Sources: UGC - National Fellowship for SC students | https://ugc.gov.in | Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (also known as SHRESHTA; other names: SHRESHTA Scheme; scheme of grant-in-aid to voluntary organisations for SC education) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: Ministry's SHRESHTA cell with NTA (National Testing Agency) for selection test; NGO-run residential schools for Mode-2. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (formerly grant-in-aid scheme). Launched: 2021-22 (renamed from the scheme of grant-in-aid to voluntary organisations working for SCs, which dates back to the 1950s-60s). Operational period: 2021-22 onwards (extended in 15th Finance Commission period). Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organisations working for Scheduled Castes. Target group: SC students in Class 9 and Class 11 in service-deficient SC-dominant areas and aspirational districts. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Age appropriate for Class 9 / Class 11 admission. Income limit: Annual family income limit as prescribed in SHRESHTA guidelines (generally up to Rs 2.5 lakh per annum - confirm current norms). Eligibility: SC student studying in government/government-aided school; selection through the SHRESHTA Selection Test conducted by NTA (Mode-1); merit-based admission to top residential high schools Not eligible / conditions: Available only for Class 9 and Class 11 entry points; students must stay in the residential school and maintain academic progress Benefits: Free high-quality residential education - full tuition, boarding and lodging, books, uniforms and other expenses in top CBSE residential schools, for the entire school course Benefit type: Education; Hostel; Scholarship. Headline benefit value: Full cost of education including tuition, food, lodging and books; about 2,200 SC students selected per year in Mode-1 across States/UTs. Funding pattern: 100% Central. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 2,200 students per year under Mode-1 plus NGO/institution grants under Mode-2. How to apply: Online registration for the SHRESHTA Selection Test (NTA), then Merit-based counselling for school allotment via shreshta.nta.ac.in / socialjustice.gov.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate; Class 8/Class 10 marksheet and school certificate; Aadhaar; bank details; photograph; school/government verification. Helpline/contact: NTA SHRESHTA helpdesk; Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. Key features: Gives SC children from SC-dominant areas access to elite residential schools; admission through an all-India selection test; free education up to Class 12 Recent updates: Selection test conducted yearly by NTA; Mode-2 (NGO-run schools) funded through the e-Anudaan portal; seats and participating schools expanded since 2023 Sources: SHRESHTA - Social Justice & Empowerment | https://socialjustice.gov.in/schemes/109 | NTA SHRESHTA portal | https://shreshta.nta.ac.in.

title: Free Coaching Scheme for Scheduled Caste and Other Backward Class Students (Free Coaching SC/OBC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Free Coaching Scheme for Scheduled Caste and Other Backward Class Students (also known as Free Coaching SC/OBC; other names: Free coaching SC OBC; coaching scheme for SC students) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: Empanelled coaching institutions; grants released through the Ministry/nodal agencies. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 2009-10 (guidelines revised 2016 and 2021). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: Economically disadvantaged SC and OBC students preparing for competitive examinations and professional courses. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines. Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 8,00,000 for SC/OBC applicants (verify latest ceiling). Eligibility: SC/OBC candidate whose family income is within the limit; should be preparing for exams such as civil services, SSC, banking, railways, State PSC, CLAT, JEE, NEET etc.; coaching through empanelled institutes for a maximum of one course/attempt slot Not eligible / conditions: Only a limited number of slots per family/beneficiary; students already getting similar coaching under another government scheme may not be eligible to repeat Benefits: Free coaching (up to 12 months) by empanelled institutes, free study material, and a monthly stipend for out-of-pocket expenses for SC/OBC students attending coaching Benefit type: Coaching; Education; Stipend. Headline benefit value: 100% cost of coaching paid to the institute (normally up to Rs 40,000-60,000 per course) plus monthly stipend of about Rs 3,000 for outstation candidates; about 3,000+ SC/OBC students per year. Funding pattern: 100% Central. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 3,000 students per year across coaching categories. How to apply: Online application on the Ministry/NSP portal, allotment to empanelled institute via scholarships.gov.in / socialjustice.gov.in (e-Anudaan). Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate; educational qualification proof; Aadhaar; bank account of student; admission/test details of target examination. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment coaching cell. Key features: Covers UPSC/SSC/banking/State PSC coaching and professional entrance exams; stipend for out-of-pocket expenses; government empanelled institutes only Recent updates: Income ceiling raised to Rs 8 lakh; list of covered examinations expanded; allocations increased in the last three Union Budgets Sources: Social Justice & Empowerment - Free Coaching | https://socialjustice.gov.in | e-Anudaan portal | https://eanudaan.socialjustice.gov.in.

title: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (also known as PM-AJAY; other names: PM AJAY; Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana; PMAGY SCA SCSP merged scheme) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (villages and institutions). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: State Governments, District Administrations, State SC Development Corporations, NIRF-ranked institutions. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme (100% central assistance to States/UTs). Launched: FY 2021-22 (merged three older schemes). Operational period: 2021-22 to 2025-26 (extended with the 15th Finance Commission period; continuing). Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCA to SCSP); Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY); Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY). Target group: SC families living below the poverty line; SC-majority villages; SC students needing hostels in top institutions. Beneficiary type: Family; Village; Institution. Age criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines. Income limit: Income Generating and Skill Development components - SC families below the poverty line; infrastructure component - SC-majority villages. Eligibility: Three components: (1) Adarsh Gram - villages with more than 40% SC population and total population of 500 or more; (2) Grants-in-aid for district/State-level projects including infrastructure in villages with 50% or more SC population and Comprehensive Livelihood Projects; (3) Construction/repair of hostels in institutions funded by Central/State/UT Governments and ranked under NIRF Not eligible / conditions: Villages and beneficiaries must be selected through the State/District Annual Action Plan on the PM-AJAY portal; projects outside the approved plan are not eligible Benefits: Integrated development of SC-dominant villages (drinking water, sanitation, education, health, roads, livelihood); grants for livelihood and skill projects for BPL SC families; financial support of up to Rs 50,000 or 50% of asset cost (whichever is less) per beneficiary for livelihood assets; hostel construction in top institutions Benefit type: Infrastructure; Livelihood; Skill; Housing-related; Education. Headline benefit value: Adarsh Gram component: gap-filling grants per village. Livelihood component: asset grant up to Rs 50,000 or 50% of cost per beneficiary household. Fund shares: up to 50% for Adarsh Gram, up to 2% for hostels, up to 5% for administration/monitoring. At least 15% of grants are to be used for income-generating schemes for SC women, at least 10% for skill development and up to 30% for infrastructure. Funding pattern: 100% central assistance (Centrally Sponsored Scheme; States meet implementation establishment costs). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: 29,881 villages covered under the Adarsh Gram component, of which 6,087 villages have been declared 'Adarsh Gram'; over Rs 3,242 crore released for livelihood projects benefiting over 8.5 lakh beneficiaries. How to apply: Through States/Districts (Annual Action Plans uploaded on the PM-AJAY portal); beneficiaries identified by State/District administration and Panchayati Raj institutions via https://pmajay.dosje.gov.in. Documents needed: For beneficiaries: caste certificate, BPL/income proof, Aadhaar, bank account, project proposal. For institutions: DPR, NIRF ranking certificate, proof of government funding. Helpline/contact: PM-AJAY Programme Implementation Unit, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment; State SC Development Corporations. Key features: Umbrella scheme merging SCA-SCSP, PMAGY and BJRCY; creates model 'Adarsh Grams' in SC-majority villages; 50 monitorable socio-economic indicators; builds hostels in NIRF-ranked institutions; earmarks 15% for SC women Recent updates: Village eligibility widened from 50% to more than 40% SC population in the revised guidelines; 6,087 villages declared Adarsh Gram; hostel component restricted to top-ranked government-funded institutions Sources: PM-AJAY portal | https://pmajay.dosje.gov.in | Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment - PM-AJAY | https://socialjustice.gov.in/schemes/104 | PIB releases on PM-AJAY (2024).

title: Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (legacy) (SCA to SCSP)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (legacy) (also known as SCA to SCSP; other names: SCA SCSP; Special Component Plan; SCSP) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: State Governments/UTs. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: 1979 (Special Component Plan for SCs under the Sixth Five Year Plan era; renamed SCSP in 2011). Operational period: 1979-80 to 2021-22. Current status: Merged & renamed. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Special Component Plan for Scheduled Castes (1979). Now continued/renamed as: PM-AJAY (Grants-in-aid component) from FY 2021-22. Target group: SC families below the poverty line; SC-majority villages. Beneficiary type: Family; Village. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: SC families below the poverty line. Eligibility: 100% central assistance to States for income generating schemes, skill development and infrastructure in villages with 50% or more SC population Not eligible / conditions: Now closed - replaced by PM-AJAY component 2 Benefits: Grants to States for SC families (income generating schemes such as agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, fisheries, handicrafts, small business) and infrastructure in SC-majority villages Benefit type: Livelihood; Infrastructure; Skill. Headline benefit value: 100% central assistance, allocated to States on the basis of SC population (50% weightage) and State SCSP allocation ratio (50% weightage). Funding pattern: 100% central assistance to States (Centrally Sponsored Scheme). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Operational for over four decades; benefits in thousands of SC-majority villages. How to apply: Through State Government Annual Action Plans (scheme now closed) via Subsumed into PM-AJAY portal - https://pmajay.dosje.gov.in. Documents needed: State-level project proposals; beneficiary lists through Panchayati Raj institutions; BPL lists. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. Key features: Cornerstone of SC development funding for 40+ years; 100% central assistance; evolved into PM-AJAY in 2021; historical data available for time-series questions Recent updates: Closed for fresh sanctions after PM-AJAY was launched in 2021-22 - treat as historical/predecessor scheme Sources: SCA to SCSP guidelines (Social Justice & Empowerment) | https://socialjustice.gov.in/writereaddata/UploadFile/Guidelines-SCA%20to%20SCSP.pdf | PM-AJAY guidelines | https://pmajay.dosje.gov.in.

title: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (legacy) (PMAGY)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (legacy) (also known as PMAGY; other names: PM Adarsh Gram Yojana SC; Adarsh Gram for SC villages) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: State Governments/UTs and Gram Panchayats. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: 2009-10 (pilot), scaled up in 2010-11; restructured 2014-15. Operational period: 2010-11 to 2021-22. Current status: Merged & renamed. Now continued/renamed as: PM-AJAY (Adarsh Gram component), 2021-22. Target group: Villages with more than 50% SC population and total population of 500 or more (later 40% norms under PM-AJAY). Beneficiary type: Village. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: Not applicable. Eligibility: Village must have SC population above 50% (PMAGY norms) and population of at least 500; selection in descending order of SC population Not eligible / conditions: Scheme closed for new villages; ongoing works subsumed under PM-AJAY Benefits: Gap-filling infrastructure grants per village to develop SC-majority villages into model villages with basic amenities Benefit type: Infrastructure. Headline benefit value: Rs 21 lakh per village (Rs 20 lakh central share + Rs 1 lakh State share) under PMAGY norms. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 90:10 earlier revised to 100% central assistance in later phases. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Villages spread across 570 districts of 25 States/UTs were identified; over 29,000 villages later covered under PM-AJAY's Adarsh Gram component. How to apply: Through State/District administration (scheme closed; now via PM-AJAY) via https://pmajay.dosje.gov.in. Documents needed: Village-level plan, SC population certificate, Gram Sabha resolution, utilisation certificates. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment / State Social Welfare Department. Key features: First dedicated SC-village infrastructure scheme; used Census-based SC concentration criteria; became the template for PM-AJAY's Adarsh Gram component Recent updates: Merged into PM-AJAY from 2021-22; PM-AJAY has now covered 29,881 villages, declaring 6,087 as Adarsh Gram Sources: PM-AJAY (Adarsh Gram) guidelines | https://socialjustice.gov.in/schemes/104 | PIB background on PMAGY and PM-AJAY.

title: Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (legacy hostel scheme) (BJRCY)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (legacy hostel scheme) (also known as BJRCY; other names: BJRCY hostel scheme; SC hostels scheme) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: States/UTs and institutions. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: Hostels for SC girls since the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66); separate SC boys' hostels from 1989-90; BJRCY named/revamped in 2007-08. Operational period: 1961-62 onwards to 2021-22 (as standalone). Current status: Merged & renamed. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Scheme of hostels for SC girls (1961) and SC boys (1989-90). Now continued/renamed as: PM-AJAY Component 3 (hostels) from 2021-22. Target group: SC students, especially girls, from rural and remote areas pursuing secondary and higher education. Beneficiary type: Student; Institution. Age criteria: School/college going age. Income limit: As prescribed for hostel admission (generally low-income SC families). Eligibility: SC students studying in middle schools, higher secondary schools, colleges and universities; hostels built by State Governments, universities, or NGOs with central assistance Not eligible / conditions: Now operated under PM-AJAY; new standalone BJRCY sanctions discontinued Benefits: Construction and repair of hostel buildings with dormitories and common facilities so that SC students, particularly girls, can study away from home Benefit type: Hostel; Education; Infrastructure. Headline benefit value: Central assistance of Rs 21 lakh per 100-seat hostel block (norm under older guidelines) plus provisions for repair/maintenance; current hostels built under PM-AJAY component 3. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 50:50 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States, as per norms of the period). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of hostel seats created for SC boys and girls across States over six decades. How to apply: Through State Government/institution proposals (now through PM-AJAY portal) via https://pmajay.dosje.gov.in. Documents needed: DPR, land documents, institutional registration, government funding proof, cost estimate, utilisation certificate. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment / State Social Welfare Department. Key features: Six-decade-old hostel programme; priority to SC girls' hostels; merged into PM-AJAY in 2021-22 Recent updates: Subsumed into PM-AJAY; PM-AJAY now allows hostel construction in NIRF-ranked government-funded higher education institutions and government schools Sources: PM-AJAY guidelines (hostel component) | https://socialjustice.gov.in/schemes/104 | Social Justice & Empowerment archived BJRCY page | https://socialjustice.nic.in.

title: Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages (DAFSICM)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (implemented by Dr. Ambedkar Foundation)
text: Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages (also known as DAFSICM; other names: Inter-caste marriage incentive central; Dr Ambedkar inter-caste marriage scheme) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (implemented by Dr. Ambedkar Foundation). Implementing agency: Dr. Ambedkar Foundation and State Governments. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 2013 (revised guidelines 2020-21). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: Inter-caste married couples where one spouse belongs to a Scheduled Caste. Beneficiary type: Couple / Family. Age criteria: Groom must be at least 21 and bride at least 18 years at marriage. Income limit: Combined annual income of the couple up to Rs 5,00,000. Eligibility: The marriage must be the first marriage of both spouses; one spouse must be SC; the couple must apply within one year of marriage with marriage certificate and caste certificates; a maximum of 500 couples are supported per year Not eligible / conditions: Couples whose marriage is not legally registered/solemnised; second marriages; applications beyond one year of marriage (unless relaxed) Benefits: One-time financial incentive of Rs 2,50,000 per couple (paid as incentive to the couple after verification) to encourage social integration and reduce caste-based exclusion Benefit type: Cash incentive; Social integration. Headline benefit value: Rs 2,50,000 per couple; up to 500 couples per year. Funding pattern: 100% Central (Dr. Ambedkar Foundation). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Up to 500 couples per year (scheme oversubscribed; States also run their own inter-caste marriage incentives). How to apply: Online/offline application through the State Social Welfare Department or Dr. Ambedkar Foundation via https://socialjustice.gov.in (Dr. Ambedkar Foundation). Documents needed: Marriage certificate; caste certificates of both spouses; income certificate; age proof; Aadhaar and bank details; joint photograph; affidavit that it is the first marriage. Helpline/contact: Dr. Ambedkar Foundation, New Delhi. Key features: Cash incentive for inter-caste marriages involving an SC spouse; 500 couples per year; States like Tamil Nadu and Karnataka give additional gold/cash incentives Recent updates: Guidelines revised to require online submission and quicker verification; demand consistently exceeds the 500-couple cap Sources: Dr. Ambedkar Foundation scheme page | https://socialjustice.gov.in | PIB write-ups on Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration.

title: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (also known as VCF-SC; other names: Venture Capital Fund SC; IFCI SC fund) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: IFCI Ltd. as sponsor/asset management company; fund registered with SEBI under AIF Regulations 2012. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (fund-based). Launched: 2014-15 (initial corpus Rs 200 crore; fund size later enhanced to about Rs 500 crore). Operational period: 2014-15 onwards. Current status: Active. Target group: SC entrepreneurs and SC-majority companies (manufacturing and services). Beneficiary type: Entrepreneur; Company. Age criteria: 18 years and above (promoter). Income limit: No income limit (enterprise-based). Eligibility: Company/enterprise with at least 51% SC shareholding and management control (12 months for loans above Rs 50 lakh; 6 months for loans up to Rs 50 lakh); manufacturing or services sector with asset creation; SC promoters must retain at least 51-60% stake until exit Not eligible / conditions: Trading-only and non-asset-creating proposals; promoters unwilling to bring the prescribed margin (25%) Benefits: Concessional equity/quasi-equity financing for SC entrepreneurs to set up or expand businesses and create jobs Benefit type: Loan; Equity; Entrepreneurship. Headline benefit value: Assistance from about Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore per company. Up to Rs 5 crore: fund invests up to 75% of project cost, promoters bring 25%. Above Rs 5 crore: fund invests up to 50%, at least 25% from bank/FI and 25% from promoters. Funding pattern: 100% Government of India corpus through IFCI-managed SEBI-registered fund. Interest rate: Concessional - as decided by the Asset Management Company (below market rates; subsidy on interest considered in evaluations). Repayment: Structured exits over about 6 years (equity/quasi-equity with defined exit). Scale/coverage reported by government: Loans of about Rs 354 crore sanctioned to 98 SC entrepreneur companies across 17 States (evaluation data); portfolio includes solar power, food processing, packaging and hotels. How to apply: Online application and appraisal by IFCI/the fund manager via https://www.vcfsc.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate of promoters; shareholding pattern proof; project report/DPR; audited financials; bank sanction letter for the loan portion; KYC and company registration documents. Helpline/contact: VCF-SC / IFCI Ltd., New Delhi. Key features: Largest dedicated venture/equity fund for SC entrepreneurs; loans from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore; preference to SC women entrepreneurs; managed professionally by IFCI under SEBI AIF rules Recent updates: Fund size enhanced; renewed push in 2024-26 towards technology-driven manufacturing ventures; scheme reviewed for expanding outreach to smaller towns Sources: VCF-SC portal | https://www.vcfsc.in | Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment VCF-SC executive summary | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: Ambedkar Social Innovation and Incubation Mission (ASIIM)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Ambedkar Social Innovation and Incubation Mission (also known as ASIIM; other names: ASIIM startup funding SC; SC startup mission) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) / IFCI with Technology Business Incubators. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (fund-based). Launched: FY 2021-22. Operational period: 2021-22 to 2025-26 (5-year plan). Current status: Active. Target group: SC students/start-up founders with innovative ideas, identified through Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) of institutions. Beneficiary type: Entrepreneur; Startup. Age criteria: Not specified (students/young entrepreneurs). Income limit: No income limit. Eligibility: SC founder-backed start-ups/innovations selected through TBIs and incubators; idea should be scalable and commercially viable Not eligible / conditions: Non-SC majority ventures; ideas without incubation validation Benefits: Equity funding in tranches to convert SC student start-up ideas into commercial ventures, with continued support of up to Rs 15 crore from VCF-SC for successful ventures Benefit type: Equity; Startup funding; Entrepreneurship. Headline benefit value: Up to Rs 30 lakh over 3 years as equity funding (in tranches of about Rs 10 lakh) per start-up; plan to support about 1,250 start-up ideas and 90 projects with Rs 350 crore over 5 years. Funding pattern: 100% Central. Interest rate: Not applicable (equity). Repayment: Not applicable (equity investment with exit). Scale/coverage reported by government: Target of about 1,250 start-up ideas and 90 funded projects during 2021-26. How to apply: Application through participating Technology Business Incubators and the VCF-SC portal via https://www.vcfsc.in/asiim/. Documents needed: Caste certificate; proof of SC majority ownership; start-up pitch/innovation proposal; incubator nomination; incorporation/registration proof. Helpline/contact: VCF-SC / IFCI ASIIM desk. Key features: First dedicated start-up funding mission for SC founders; funds ideas from student stage; links incubation to venture funding Recent updates: Continued under VCF-SC in 2024-26; focus on tech manufacturing, agri-tech and service innovations Sources: ASIIM page | https://www.vcfsc.in/asiim/ | VCF-SC scheme document | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme for Scheduled Castes (CEGS-SC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme for Scheduled Castes (also known as CEGS-SC; other names: Credit enhancement SC; guarantee scheme SC entrepreneurs) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: IFCI Ltd./designated nodal agency providing credit guarantees to banks. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 2014-15 (budget announcement 2014; operational from 2015-16). Operational period: 2015-16 onwards. Current status: Active. Target group: SC entrepreneurs/companies (including first-generation entrepreneurs) needing bank credit without adequate collateral. Beneficiary type: Entrepreneur. Age criteria: 18 years and above. Income limit: Normally linked to the definition of SC families within income limits for credit schemes (verify current norm). Eligibility: SC entrepreneur/company with at least 51% SC shareholding; viable project appraised by a bank/financial institution; the guarantee is issued in favour of the lending bank Not eligible / conditions: Defaults and wilful non-repayment lead to guarantee invocation and recovery action; not a subsidy Benefits: Guarantee cover to banks so that SC entrepreneurs with viable projects can get credit without collateral, improving access to institutional finance Benefit type: Credit guarantee; Loan facilitation. Headline benefit value: Guarantee cover on sanctioned loans as per the guidelines (initial scheme corpus Rs 200 crore; guarantees enabling credit to SC entrepreneurs). Confirm individual limits with IFCI/the nodal agency. Funding pattern: 100% Central. Interest rate: Not applicable (guarantee fee instead of interest). Repayment: As per the underlying bank loan. Scale/coverage reported by government: Cumulative guarantee support to SC entrepreneurs across States since 2015-16. How to apply: Application routed through the lending bank to the nodal agency (IFCI) via https://socialjustice.gov.in (Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme). Documents needed: Caste certificate; SC shareholding proof; project report; bank appraisal/loan sanction details; financial statements; KYC documents. Helpline/contact: IFCI Ltd. / Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. Key features: Addresses the biggest barrier for SC entrepreneurs - collateral; works with banks rather than as a subsidy; complements VCF-SC and NSSH Recent updates: Being dovetailed with other SC entrepreneurship schemes (VCF-SC, National SC-ST Hub) in recent budget announcements; verification of current limits advised Sources: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment - Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation - Term Loan Schemes (NSFDC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation - Term Loan Schemes (also known as NSFDC; other names: NSFDC loan scheme; SC corporation loan; term loan for SC) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (through State Channelizing Agencies). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: NSFDC through State SC Development Corporations/Channelizing Agencies, regional rural banks and public sector banks. Scheme type: Corporation credit scheme (Government company under Section 8 of the Companies Act). Launched: 1989 (NSFDC set up; renamed from National Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation). Operational period: 1989 onwards. Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: National Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (1989). Target group: SC families living below double the poverty line (DPL) - artisans, petty traders, transport operators, small entrepreneurs, women. Beneficiary type: Individual; Family; Entrepreneur; SHG. Age criteria: 18 to 55 years (relaxable for specific schemes). Income limit: Annual family income up to double the poverty line (DPL) as notified (about Rs 1.5 lakh rural / Rs 1.8 lakh urban in recent norms - confirm current DPL). Eligibility: SC individual/SHG/cooperative with viable income-generating activity; applications routed through State Channelizing Agencies or partner banks; no existing default with any bank/FI Not eligible / conditions: Wilful defaulters; activities prohibited under applicable law; applicants above income ceiling Benefits: Concessional term loans (up to 90-95% of unit cost) for self-employment and income-generating activities, with training and market support Benefit type: Loan; Livelihood; Entrepreneurship; Skill. Headline benefit value: Term loan up to Rs 30 lakh per unit (Small loans up to Rs 1 lakh; Medium Rs 1-5 lakh; Large Rs 5-30 lakh); beneficiaries pay about 5-6% interest; NSFDC charges State agencies a lower rate. Funding pattern: NSFDC equity from Government of India; on-lending through State Channelizing Agencies. Interest rate: About 5% to 6% per annum for beneficiaries (differs by scheme category and State agency). Repayment: Monthly/quarterly instalments over 3 to 10 years including moratorium, depending on the scheme. Scale/coverage reported by government: Large portfolio - NSFDC has financed lakhs of SC beneficiaries since 1989 (ask for the current sanction/disbursement figures on the NSFDC dashboard). How to apply: Offline/online application through State SC Development Corporation (Channelizing Agency) or designated bank branch; some schemes via the NSFDC portal via https://nsfdc.nic.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate / DPL certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; project/unit estimate or quotation; SHG or firm registration if applicable; no-dues declaration. Helpline/contact: NSFDC head office, New Delhi (011-26179448); State SC Development Corporation helplines. Key features: Apex Government of India credit institution for SCs; interest well below market rates; works through State channel agencies; combines credit with skill training and market linkage; covers micro-credit to large term loans Recent updates: NSFDC has expanded digital application, credit-guarantee tie-ups and the Green Business Scheme (e-rickshaw, solar pumps, poly houses) in 2024-26 Sources: NSFDC official site | https://nsfdc.nic.in | Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment - NSFDC | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: Mahila Samridhi Yojana (NSFDC micro-finance for SC women) (MSY)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Mahila Samridhi Yojana (NSFDC micro-finance for SC women) (also known as MSY; other names: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana; SC women microfinance loan) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (through State Channelizing Agencies). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: NSFDC through State Channelizing Agencies/micro-finance institutions. Scheme type: Corporation micro-credit scheme. Launched: 1990s (continuously revised; now with 4% interest for SC women). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC women entrepreneurs below double the poverty line, including SHG members. Beneficiary type: Woman; Entrepreneur; SHG. Age criteria: 18 to 55 years. Income limit: Family income within double the poverty line. Eligibility: SC woman with a viable micro-enterprise plan or SHG undertaking group activity; routed through the State Channelizing Agency Not eligible / conditions: Defaulters; proposals without viable unit economics Benefits: Micro-credit for SC women to set up or expand micro-enterprises with training and follow-up support, at highly concessional interest Benefit type: Micro-credit; Livelihood; Women empowerment. Headline benefit value: Project cost up to Rs 1,40,000; loan up to Rs 1,25,000 (about 90% of cost); SC women pay about 4% interest per annum; repayment is short-term (about 3 to 3.5 years including moratorium). Funding pattern: NSFDC refinance to State agencies, which on-lend to beneficiaries. Interest rate: About 4% per annum for SC women beneficiaries. Repayment: Short-term loan - usually 3 to 3.5 years in quarterly instalments with a 3-6 month moratorium. Scale/coverage reported by government: Lakhs of SC women financed across States since inception. How to apply: Through State SC Development Corporation / Channelizing Agency; also via SHG federations via https://nsfdc.nic.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income proof; Aadhaar; bank account; SHG membership proof; activity/business estimate; photograph. Helpline/contact: NSFDC head office (011-26179448); State SC Development Corporation. Key features: Exclusive micro-finance window for SC women at about 4% interest; small ticket size suits home-based businesses; builds credit history for first-time borrowers Recent updates: Digital onboarding with Aadhaar; convergence with SHG platforms in several States; interest subvention in select States Sources: NSFDC schemes | https://nsfdc.nic.in | Vikaspedia - NSFDC scheme profile | https://vikaspedia.in.

title: NSFDC Green Business Scheme (GBS (NSFDC))
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: NSFDC Green Business Scheme (also known as GBS (NSFDC); other names: Green Business Scheme; e-rickshaw loan SC; solar pump loan SC) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: NSFDC through State Channelizing Agencies. Scheme type: Corporation credit scheme. Launched: 2016 (in response to climate-change concerns and to promote green livelihoods). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC persons setting up green/climate-friendly micro-enterprises. Beneficiary type: Individual; Entrepreneur. Age criteria: 18 years and above. Income limit: Family income within double the poverty line. Eligibility: SC applicant proposing activities such as e-rickshaw, solar pump, solar-powered implements, poly-house, waste recycling; unit cost within the prescribed limit Not eligible / conditions: Diesel-based or non-green activities; defaulters Benefits: Concessional loan for green livelihood assets, generating income with low running cost Benefit type: Loan; Livelihood; Green enterprise. Headline benefit value: Loan for unit cost up to about Rs 1 lakh at concessional interest (about 5% per annum). Funding pattern: NSFDC refinance through State Channelizing Agencies. Interest rate: Concessional (about 5% per annum for beneficiaries). Repayment: Term loan over about 3 to 5 years with moratorium. Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of green livelihood units financed; e-rickshaw financing is the largest segment. How to apply: Through State SC Development Corporation / Channelizing Agency via https://nsfdc.nic.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; quotation/invoice of the asset; driving licence for e-rickshaw. Helpline/contact: NSFDC head office; State SC Development Corporation. Key features: Ties SC livelihood support to clean energy transition; low unit cost hence easier entry for first-generation entrepreneurs Recent updates: Expanded in 2024-26 with solar pump and e-mobility financing in rural districts Sources: Vikaspedia - NSFDC Green Business Scheme | https://vikaspedia.in | NSFDC | https://nsfdc.nic.in.

title: NSFDC Educational Loan and Vocational Education & Training Loan Scheme (NSFDC Edu Loan / VETLS)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: NSFDC Educational Loan and Vocational Education & Training Loan Scheme (also known as NSFDC Edu Loan / VETLS; other names: NSFDC education loan; vocational training loan SC) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: NSFDC through State Channelizing Agencies and banks. Scheme type: Corporation credit scheme. Launched: Educational loan scheme revised through the 2010s; VETLS introduced for short-term courses. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC students pursuing professional/technical education and short-term vocational courses. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: 18 to 55 years. Income limit: Family income within double the poverty line (relaxed for some courses). Eligibility: SC student with confirmed admission to a recognised professional/technical course (in India or abroad) or a short-term vocational training course Not eligible / conditions: Courses not recognised by the relevant regulator; students with existing education-loan default Benefits: Concessional education loan covering course fees and related expenses for professional/technical education, and small loans for short-term vocational training Benefit type: Education loan; Skill. Headline benefit value: Educational loan as per NSFDC norms (up to Rs 15-30 lakh for professional courses in India/abroad depending on the scheme); VETLS loan about Rs 4 lakh for short courses with 4% interest for male and 3.5% for female awardees. Funding pattern: NSFDC refinance through State Channelizing Agencies. Interest rate: About 4% per annum for men and 3.5% per annum for women under VETLS; concessional rates for education loans. Repayment: Starts after six months of completing the course or on employment, whichever is earlier (VETLS); education loans have longer repayment with moratorium. Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of SC students financed for professional and vocational courses. How to apply: Through State SC Development Corporation / Channelizing Agency via https://nsfdc.nic.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income proof; admission letter/fee receipt; academic marksheets; co-obligant details if required; Aadhaar and bank account. Helpline/contact: NSFDC head office; State SC Development Corporation. Key features: Interest concession for women; supports both degree-level professional courses and short-term employable training; complements the Post-Matric Scholarship for students outside the income ceiling Recent updates: Convergence with Skill India/PM-DAKSH short-course skilling in recent years Sources: NSFDC schemes | https://nsfdc.nic.in | State SC Development Corporation scheme listings (e.g. HP/Chandigarh SC corporations).

title: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation schemes (NSKFDC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation schemes (also known as NSKFDC; other names: NSKFDC loan; safai karamchari loan scheme; sanitation worker credit) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (through State Channelizing Agencies). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: NSKFDC through State Channelizing Agencies, banks and NGOs. Scheme type: Corporation credit scheme (Government of India company). Launched: 1997 (NSKFDC incorporated). Operational period: 1997 onwards. Current status: Active. Target group: Safai karamcharis (sanitation workers) and their dependents, and persons engaged in manual scavenging identified under law - predominantly SC but open to all such workers. Beneficiary type: Individual; Woman; SHG; Entrepreneur. Age criteria: 18 to 55 years (relaxable in specific cases). Income limit: Family income within prescribed limits (about double the poverty line / low-income households). Eligibility: Safai karamchari or dependent/legal heir; proposed activity should be viable; applications routed through State Channelizing Agencies or banks Not eligible / conditions: Wilful defaulters; activities without income-generation potential; non-target groups Benefits: Term loans at concessional rates for self-employment, small business, transport, education and skill up-gradation; also sanitation-related enterprise finance Benefit type: Loan; Livelihood; Education; Skill; Entrepreneurship. Headline benefit value: Term loans up to Rs 30 lakh depending on the scheme (Small up to Rs 1 lakh; Medium up to Rs 5 lakh; Large above Rs 5 lakh); interest about 5-6% per annum for beneficiaries; VETLS-type short-term loans with 3.5-4% interest. Funding pattern: NSKFDC equity from Government of India; refinance through SCAs and banks. Interest rate: About 5% (men) and 4-5% (women) per annum, scheme-wise. Repayment: 3 to 10 years in monthly/quarterly instalments with moratorium. Scale/coverage reported by government: Lakhs of sanitation workers and their families financed; ~Rs 1,000+ crore loan portfolio over the years. How to apply: Through State Channelizing Agencies/direct lending through banks; application form on the NSKFDC portal via https://nskfdc.nic.in. Documents needed: Safai karamchari certificate/employment proof; caste certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; project report; identity proof. Helpline/contact: NSKFDC head office, New Delhi; State Channelizing Agency helplines. Key features: Only national corporation dedicated to sanitation workers' credit needs; includes education loans for children of safai karamcharis; prioritises liberation from hereditary sanitation work Recent updates: Coordinated with NAMASTE (2022) and the SRMS rehabilitation scheme; NSKFDC supports capital subsidy and skill components of NAMASTE Sources: NSKFDC official site | https://nskfdc.nic.in | Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (now under NAMASTE) (SRMS / NAMASTE)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for the NAMASTE sewer/septic tank component)
text: Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (now under NAMASTE) (also known as SRMS / NAMASTE; other names: SRMS; NAMASTE scheme; rehabilitation of manual scavengers scheme) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for the NAMASTE sewer/septic tank component). Implementing agency: NSKFDC and State Governments/Urban Local Bodies. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored / Central Sector Scheme. Launched: SRMS 2007 (revised 2013); NAMASTE launched in 2022-23 as the upgraded umbrella. Operational period: 2007 onwards; NAMASTE from 2022-23 to 2025-26 (extended). Current status: Active (SRMS subsumed in NAMASTE). Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: National Scheme for Liberation and Rehabilitation of Scavengers (NSLRS, 1992). Now continued/renamed as: NAMASTE - National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (2022). Target group: Identified manual scavengers, sewer/septic tank workers (sanitation workers) and their dependents. Beneficiary type: Individual; Family; Woman; Entrepreneur. Age criteria: 18 years and above. Income limit: No separate income ceiling - eligibility based on identification as manual scavenger/sanitation worker. Eligibility: Person identified/verified as a manual scavenger or sewer/septic tank worker (or dependent), with a certificate from the district administration; one-time rehabilitation assistance applies once per family Not eligible / conditions: Families that have already received the one-time cash assistance under SRMS; persons not in the verified list unless newly identified Benefits: One-time cash assistance, skill training, concessional loans/entrepreneurship support, education support for children, and mechanised sanitation equipment (NAMASTE) for sanitation workers' safety and dignity Benefit type: Cash assistance; Skill; Loan; Livelihood; Education; Occupational safety. Headline benefit value: One-time cash assistance of Rs 40,000 per identified manual scavenger (SRMS); loans up to Rs 15 lakh for sanitation enterprises with capital subsidy up to Rs 5 lakh (NAMASTE/NSKFDC norms); NAMASTE also funds PPE kits, mechanised cleaning equipment and safety devices; budget for NAMASTE components enhanced in recent Union Budgets. Funding pattern: Central assistance with State/ULB participation; NSKFDC as the financial intermediary. Interest rate: Concessional on loans (about 4-5% per annum for beneficiaries). Repayment: As per the linked loan scheme (3 to 10 years). Scale/coverage reported by government: Over 1 lakh manual scavengers identified and given rehabilitation assistance since 2013; NAMASTE targets safety and mechanisation for all sanitation workers in urban local bodies. How to apply: Through District Administration/Municipal bodies and State Channelizing Agencies; applications verified against the national survey list via https://nskfdc.nic.in / https://namaste.mohua.gov.in. Documents needed: Manual scavenger/sanitation worker identification certificate; caste certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; income/project details; dependant proof if applicable. Helpline/contact: NSKFDC / NAMASTE helpline; State Sanitation/Social Welfare Department. Key features: Rehabilitation (not just compensation) of sanitation workers; covers cash, skill, credit, education and safety equipment; implemented jointly with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs after 2022 Recent updates: NAMASTE launched in 2022-23 with mechanised cleaning, PPE and enterprise support; Union Budget 2025-26 enhanced sanitation-worker welfare and capital subsidy components Sources: NAMASTE scheme (MoHUA) | https://namaste.mohua.gov.in | NSKFDC / SRMS documentation | https://nskfdc.nic.in.

title: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (PCR-PoA Scheme)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (also known as PCR-PoA Scheme; other names: SC ST PoA implementation scheme; atrocity relief scheme; special courts scheme) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: State Governments/UTs, police, special courts and district administrations. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: 1989 Act; supporting scheme funded continuously since the 1990s (revised guidelines 2016 and later). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC and ST victims of atrocities and their dependents; institutions enforcing protective laws. Beneficiary type: Individual; Family; Institution. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: No income ceiling for relief to atrocity victims. Eligibility: Victim must be an SC/ST person covered under the PCR Act 1955 or the SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989; relief is based on the offence category under the PoA Rules (47 listed offences); FIR/police report and court/medical documentation required Not eligible / conditions: Relief amounts differ by offence and may be paid in instalments; the scheme funds institutions, not a general grant for individual applicants Benefits: Financial relief and rehabilitation for atrocity victims and dependents, incentive for inter-caste marriages involving SC/ST victims, funds for special courts, special public prosecutors, protection cells and atrocity-prone-village preventive measures Benefit type: Legal-relief; Rehabilitation; Cash assistance; Institutional support. Headline benefit value: Relief range of Rs 85,000 to Rs 8.25 lakh depending on the offence (e.g. Rs 5 lakh for rape, Rs 8.25 lakh for gang rape/acid attack or murder; Rs 1 lakh for caste abuse/denial of entry), payable within 7 days of the incident in stages; States may pay higher (Tamil Nadu raised to Rs 1-12 lakh). A government task force has recommended raising these amounts for inflation. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 50:50 Centre:State for most components; 100% for some components (special courts, prosecutors) as per guidelines. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Relief paid to tens of thousands of atrocity victims/dependents; special courts and exclusive special courts established in States/UTs. How to apply: Through police, district administration/District Magistrate (relief), and State Social Welfare Department; courts can also order relief via https://socialjustice.gov.in (SC/ST PoA scheme); State SC/ST protection cells. Documents needed: FIR/crime records; caste certificate of victim; medical report where applicable; identity proof; bank account; dependants' proof; court orders if available. Helpline/contact: State SC/ST Protection Cell; National Commission for Scheduled Castes; District Magistrate's office. Key features: Funds the entire protective-legal architecture for SC/ST communities; 47 offence categories mapped to relief amounts; 7-day mandate for first instalment; includes preventive measures in atrocity-prone villages; inter-caste marriage incentive for SC/ST victims is a separate component Recent updates: Task force (report submitted July 2026) recommended inflation-linked enhancement of relief amounts, counselling for victims/accused, relief cells in every State/UT and 24-hour reporting of FIRs/chargesheets to officials Sources: Social Justice & Empowerment - PCR and PoA implementation scheme | https://socialjustice.gov.in | PIB and The Hindu reports on task-force recommendations (2026) | https://www.thehindu.com.

title: Information-Monitoring, Evaluation and Social Audit (formerly Information and Mass Education) scheme (I-MESA)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Information-Monitoring, Evaluation and Social Audit (formerly Information and Mass Education) scheme (also known as I-MESA; other names: I MESA scheme; information mass education scheme SC development) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: Ministry with partner agencies and States for social-audit pilots. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: Renamed as I-MESA in 2021-22 (Information and Mass Education component runs since the 1990s). Operational period: 2021-22 to 2025-26 (part of the SC development umbrella). Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Scheme of Information and Mass Education (IME). Target group: SC/DNT communities (as information recipients); programme officials and implementing agencies (for monitoring and social audit). Beneficiary type: Community; Institution. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: Not applicable. Eligibility: Information dissemination campaigns, media/mass contact programmes, monitoring of field-level disputes, studies and social audits of SC welfare schemes Not eligible / conditions: Not a direct benefit transfer scheme for individuals Benefits: Creates awareness of government schemes among SC communities, funds monitoring of implementation, evaluation studies and social audits for accountability Benefit type: Awareness; Monitoring & evaluation; Social audit. Headline benefit value: Scheme budget under the SC development umbrella (about Rs 50 crore per year range); funds state-level IEC activities and studies. Funding pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Scheme). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: National awareness campaigns and audit studies across States/UTs. How to apply: Implemented by the Ministry with State departments, empanelled agencies and research institutions via https://socialjustice.gov.in. Documents needed: Not applicable for individuals - institutional proposals, media plans, study terms of reference. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. Key features: Umbrella for awareness, monitoring and social audit (renamed I-MESA); ensures schemes reach beneficiaries; introduces social audit for SC development programmes Recent updates: Renamed I-MESA in 2021-22 with added social-audit mandate; officials have emphasised output-based monitoring from 2024-25 Sources: Union Budget Expenditure Profile - SC development umbrella | https://www.indiabudget.gov.in | Social Justice & Empowerment scheme pages | https://socialjustice.gov.in.
