title: Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes and SC Sub-Plan strategy (DAPSC / SCSP)
ministry: Multiple Central Ministries/Departments - every Ministry earmarks funds; monitored by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
text: Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes and SC Sub-Plan strategy (also known as DAPSC / SCSP; other names: SC Sub Plan; Special Component Plan; 41 ministries SC earmarking) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Multiple Central Ministries/Departments - every Ministry earmarks funds; monitored by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. Implementing agency: 41 Central Ministries/Departments and State Governments. Scheme type: Budgetary strategy (not a standalone scheme). Launched: 1979 Special Component Plan by States; DAPSC adopted in 2018-19 after the 2014-15 NITI Aayog framework. Operational period: 1979 (States) and 2018-19 (Central DAPSC) onwards. Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Special Component Plan (1979); SC Sub Plan; Special Central Assistance. Target group: Scheduled Caste population covered through all centrally funded development sectors. Beneficiary type: Community. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: Not applicable. Eligibility: States must earmark SC sub-plan funds in proportion to SC population; 41 Central Ministries earmark specified shares (2-17%) of their budget under DAPSC; both allocations are supposed to be non-divertible Not eligible / conditions: Funds under DAPSC/SCSP can be used only for activities permissible under the guidelines; unspent amounts lapse/adjust as per rules Benefits: An earmarking mechanism that guarantees a share of every development sector's budget for SC welfare - education, health, roads, housing, electrification, water supply and livelihood Benefit type: Budgetary earmarking; Development. Headline benefit value: Union Budget 2025-26 allocated about Rs 13,000+ crore of DAPSC/dedicated SC funding within the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment alone; total DAPSC across 41 ministries runs into lakhs of crores over five years. Funding pattern: Earmarked share of each Ministry's budget (2% to 17%) plus State SC sub-plan funds. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Covers the entire SC population through sectoral ministries; the test is SC sub-plan utilisation, tracked annually by parliamentary committees. How to apply: Not an application-based scheme - it is an allocation/monitoring framework via https://www.indiabudget.gov.in (Statement 13B/13C SC sub-plan statements). Documents needed: Not applicable for individuals. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment / NITI Aayog. Key features: Guarantees multi-sectoral funding proportional to SC population; 41 Central Ministries covered; NITI Aayog monitors State SC sub-plans; historically the backbone of SC development finance Recent updates: Utilisation of DAPSC funds reviewed repeatedly by parliamentary committees (2024-26); emphasis on non-divergence and outcome-based monitoring; 2025-26 Budget retained the flagged SC budget streams Sources: Union Budget documents - Scheduled Caste component | https://www.indiabudget.gov.in | NITI Aayog/Standing Committee reports on DAPSC and SCSP.

title: Scheme of Assistance to Scheduled Castes Development Corporations (SCDC Assistance)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
text: Scheme of Assistance to Scheduled Castes Development Corporations (also known as SCDC Assistance; other names: SCDC scheme; assistance to SC development corporations) is a SC welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (28 SCDCs covered). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: State Scheduled Castes Development Corporations (SCDCs) with NSFDC. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 1990s; continues as a component supporting State SC corporations. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC families served through State SC Development Corporations; the SCDCs themselves. Beneficiary type: Institution; Family. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: Beneficiary families below double the poverty line (for credit routed through SCDCs). Eligibility: State SC Development Corporations receive central support for share capital, micro-credit and skill development to serve SC families; applies to States/UTs with an SCDC Not eligible / conditions: Central support is to corporations, not to individuals directly Benefits: Funds State SC Development Corporations to provide micro-credit, income-generating asset loans, skill training, and to strengthen their capacity to reach SC beneficiaries Benefit type: Micro-credit; Skill; Institutional capacity. Headline benefit value: Central share capital and support in the range of Rs 1-3 crore per State agency per cycle (varies); supports lending at 4-6% to beneficiaries. Funding pattern: 100% Central to State corporations. Interest rate: Not applicable at the scheme level; beneficiary loans through SCDCs at about 4-6%. Repayment: Not applicable at the scheme level. Scale/coverage reported by government: 28 SCDCs in States/UTs supported; they in turn reach lakhs of SC families. How to apply: Through State SC Development Corporations (for beneficiaries: walk-in applications at the SCDC/branch office or via State portals) via https://socialjustice.gov.in / respective State SCDC websites. Documents needed: For individuals: caste certificate, income proof, Aadhaar, project details. Helpline/contact: State Scheduled Castes Development Corporation helplines. Key features: Keeps the State-level delivery machinery for SC credit alive; links Central credit (NSFDC) with State-level outreach; supports field-level staff and loan monitoring Recent updates: Government has pushed SCDCs toward digital loan management and convergence with PM-AJAY grants in 2024-26 Sources: Social Justice & Empowerment - SCDC assistance | https://socialjustice.gov.in | NSFDC/State SCDC annual reports.

title: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS)
state_ut: All India (tribal blocks and areas with 50%+ ST population)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (also known as EMRS; other names: Eklavya schools; EMRS tribal residential school) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (tribal blocks and areas with 50%+ ST population). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs; construction with States/UTs. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 1997-98 (as a scheme of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs); revamped as a Central Sector Scheme from 2018-19 with NESTS. Operational period: 1997-98 onwards; major expansion 2019-20 to 2025-26. Current status: Active. Target group: ST students, especially from remote tribal areas and PVTG habitations. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: School students from Class VI to Class XII. Income limit: No income ceiling; eligibility based on ST status and residence in tribal areas; selection test/merit per State norms. Eligibility: Normally one EMRS in every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons; admission for Classes VI and XI (vacancies in other classes where available) Not eligible / conditions: Non-ST students are not eligible; students must reside in the school hostel Benefits: Free, high-quality residential education from Class VI to XII with boarding, lodging, books, uniforms, sports and extra-curricular facilities, plus skill and vocational modules Benefit type: Education; Hostel; Residential school. Headline benefit value: Fully funded school education - no fees; about 728 EMRS to be functional by March 2026, serving about 3.5 lakh tribal students; recurring cost per student met by the Centre. Funding pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Scheme); States provide land and some infrastructure. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 440 EMRS operational (2023) and about 700+ sanctioned; target of 728 functional schools with 3.5 lakh students by March 2026. How to apply: Online admission test/application notified by NESTS/State tribal department each year via https://emrs.tribal.gov.in. Documents needed: ST (caste/tribe) certificate; domicile/residence proof; Class V/VIII marksheet or school certificate; Aadhaar; photograph; income certificate (where required by State). Helpline/contact: NESTS/EMRS helpline, Ministry of Tribal Affairs (011-23073706). Key features: Flagship residential school network for tribal children; curriculum includes tribal culture and vocational skills; nationally administered through NESTS; over 600 EMRS students cleared IIT-JEE/NEET-type exams in recent years Recent updates: 40 new EMRS inaugurated in 2024-25 with foundations for 25 more; target to make 728 EMRS functional by March 2026; large share of new schools located in PVTG blocks Sources: EMRS portal - Ministry of Tribal Affairs | https://emrs.tribal.gov.in | PIB Tribal Day 2025 compendium | https://static.pib.gov.in.

title: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (PMS-ST)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (also known as PMS-ST; other names: ST post matric scholarship; post matric scholarship tribal students) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: State Governments/UTs through the National Scholarship Portal and DBT Tribal portal. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: Long-standing scheme (post-independence era); norms revised from 2012-13, rates revised 2019-20. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: ST students from Class XI to post-graduate and professional courses. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines. Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 2,50,000. Eligibility: ST student pursuing any recognised course whose minimum qualification is matriculation (Class X) or above, in a recognised institution in India Not eligible / conditions: Student must not draw any other centrally funded scholarship; failure to pass/promote leads to loss of scholarship; Aadhaar-linked DBT compulsory Benefits: Full compulsory course fees plus monthly maintenance allowance, book grant and study-tour support for ST students in secondary and higher education Benefit type: Scholarship; Fee reimbursement; Education. Headline benefit value: Maintenance allowance about Rs 230 to Rs 1,200 per month depending on course group and hosteller/day-scholar status, plus compulsory non-refundable fees; about 30 lakh ST students covered across all scholarship schemes annually. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 Centre:State (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 1.01 crore beneficiaries and Rs 13,380+ crore disbursed during 2019-20 to 2024-25; Rs 2,598 crore released in FY 2024-25 alone. How to apply: Online through the National Scholarship Portal / DBT Tribal portal with State verification via https://scholarships.gov.in / https://dbttribal.gov.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; income certificate (up to Rs 2.5 lakh); Class 10 marksheet; admission proof and fee receipt; Aadhaar-seeded bank account; Aadhaar; photo. Helpline/contact: State Tribal Welfare Department; NSP helpline 0120-6619540. Key features: Largest ST education scheme by expenditure; 100% DBT; covers professional courses as well as general degrees; Ministry has repeatedly urged States to clear pending fee dues Recent updates: Rs 2,598 crore released in FY 2024-25 vs Rs 2,669 crore in FY 2023-24; States instructed to settle institutional dues through DBT; NSP integration strengthened Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs scholarship page | https://tribal.nic.in/Scholarship.aspx | PIB release on tribal scholarships (4 Dec 2025) | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2198856.

title: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (Classes IX and X) (Pre-Matric ST)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (Classes IX and X) (also known as Pre-Matric ST; other names: ST pre matric scholarship; tribal pre-matric scholarship class 9 10) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: States/UTs through the National Scholarship Portal. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: 1990s; revised from 2012-13 with rates revised in 2019-20. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: ST students studying in Classes IX and X. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Age-appropriate for Classes IX and X. Income limit: Parental annual income from all sources up to Rs 2,50,000. Eligibility: ST student in Class IX or X in a government/government-recognised school; regular attendance and appearance in the annual examination Not eligible / conditions: Only Classes IX and X are covered; no other centrally funded scholarship of the same nature can be held simultaneously Benefits: Monthly scholarship to help ST students continue from upper-primary to secondary stage and reduce drop-out Benefit type: Scholarship; Education. Headline benefit value: Rs 225 per month for day scholars and Rs 525 per month for hostellers, for 10 months in a year (revised rates); annual book grant as applicable. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 30 lakh ST students get scholarships annually across all Ministry scholarship schemes; pre-matric covers lakhs of Class IX-X students. How to apply: Online through the National Scholarship Portal with school verification via https://scholarships.gov.in / https://dbttribal.gov.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; school admission proof/promotion certificate; photo. Helpline/contact: State Tribal Welfare Department; NSP helpline 0120-6619540. title: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students (NFST / Top Class ST)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students (also known as NFST / Top Class ST; other names: National Fellowship ST; Top Class Scholarship ST; ST research fellowship) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: Ministry of Tribal Affairs directly (Central Sector Schemes) through DBT. Scheme type: Central Sector Schemes (Fellowship + Scholarship components). Launched: Fellowship component running since 2000s with new design from 2019-20; Top Class Scholarship from 2013-14. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for ST (earlier design). Target group: Meritorious ST students pursuing higher education in premier institutes (Top Class) and MPhil/PhD (Fellowship). Beneficiary type: Student; Researcher. Age criteria: As per institute norms for the course. Income limit: Fellowship - no income ceiling; Top Class Scholarship - family income up to Rs 6 lakh per annum. Eligibility: Fellowship: 750 fresh ST scholars per year selected on merit in the Master's degree for MPhil/PhD, with preference to girls, divyangjan and PVTG candidates. Top Class: admission to prescribed courses in about 252-265 identified premier institutes (IITs, IIMs, AIIMS, NITs etc.) Not eligible / conditions: Candidates receiving another fellowship/salary cannot hold this fellowship; award requires submission of progress reports Benefits: Monthly fellowship for research scholars and, under the Top Class component, tuition and living allowance for ST students in premier institutions Benefit type: Fellowship; Scholarship; Fee reimbursement; Research. Headline benefit value: Fellowship: MPhil Rs 25,000 per month and PhD Rs 28,000 per month (as per latest rates) plus contingency; 750 fresh fellowships per year. Top Class: full tuition, living expenses, book grant and computer allowance, income ceiling Rs 6 lakh. Funding pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Schemes). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: 750 fresh fellowships per year; about 1,000 fresh Top Class scholarships per year; results/merit lists published annually on the Ministry portal. How to apply: Online through the National Fellowship portal/Digital Bharat portal; merit lists published by the Ministry via https://fellowship.tribal.gov.in / https://scholarships.gov.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; PG degree marksheets; admission/registration proof; bank details; Aadhaar; undertaking and guide's endorsement; income certificate for the Top Class component. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Tribal Affairs fellowship desk; 011-23073706. Key features: Two-in-one scheme covering premier-institute scholarships and research fellowships; preference to girls, divyang and PVTG students; paid directly to scholars via DBT Recent updates: Applications invited for the 2025-26 cycle (closing 31 October 2025); list of eligible institutes expanded to 252; merit lists published on the Ministry site Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs - Scholarship page (NFST) | https://tribal.nic.in/Scholarship.aspx | PIB release on tribal scholarships (4 Dec 2025) | https://www.pib.gov.in.

title: National Overseas Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (NOS-ST)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: National Overseas Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students (also known as NOS-ST; other names: ST overseas scholarship; tribal overseas scholarship) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: Ministry of Tribal Affairs with the Ministry of External Affairs and Indian embassies abroad. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: Running since the 2000s; guidelines revised in 2019-20 and later. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: ST students pursuing Master's, PhD and post-doctoral courses abroad. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: As per the scheme guidelines (normally below 35 years for Master's and below 40 for PhD). Income limit: Family income ceiling as prescribed in the scheme guidelines (verify current ceiling). Eligibility: ST candidate with a good academic record and confirmed admission to a recognised foreign university for a prescribed Master's/PhD/post-doctoral course; must return to India after completion Not eligible / conditions: Undergraduate courses are not covered; award is subject to the annual slot ceiling Benefits: Financial assistance covering tuition, maintenance, airfare, visa and related costs for higher studies abroad Benefit type: Scholarship; Education. Headline benefit value: Financial assistance as per NOS-ST norms; about 20 awards per year (including reserved slots for PVTG candidates); annual maintenance component comparable to the SC overseas scheme (about USD 15,400 per year) plus tuition and other grants. Funding pattern: 100% Central; funds routed through the Ministry of External Affairs/embassies. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 20 ST scholars per selection year; provisional selection lists published on the portal. How to apply: Online application through the dedicated NOS portal via https://overseas.tribal.gov.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; admission offer letter; degree marksheets; income certificate; passport; bank details; language proficiency score. title: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (coordinating 9 Central Ministries)
text: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (also known as PM-JANMAN; other names: PM JANMAN; Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan; PVTG mission) is a PVTG welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (PVTG habitations in 18 States/UTs). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (coordinating 9 Central Ministries). Implementing agency: Nine Central Ministries/Departments, State Governments and district administrations. Scheme type: Central Sector/Centrally Sponsored mission (multi-ministry convergence). Launched: 15 November 2023 (Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, from Khunti, Jharkhand). Operational period: 2023-24 to 2025-26 (with further continuation provisions); 9-year vision planning. Current status: Active. Now continued/renamed as: Extends logic to all tribal villages through DAJGUA (2024). Target group: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) - 75 PVTGs across the country. Beneficiary type: Family; Village; Community. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: No separate income ceiling; eligibility is PVTG habitation/residence. Eligibility: PVTG households in habitations identified by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (about 4.9 lakh households); benefits delivered through 11 critical interventions Not eligible / conditions: Non-PVTG households in the same village may be covered only for common infrastructure, per guidelines Benefits: Saturation of PVTG habitations with pucca houses, roads, mobile connectivity, electricity, solar power, drinking water, community water supply, education (hostels, anganwadis), health facilities, and skill/livelihood support Benefit type: Housing; Infrastructure; Livelihood; Health; Education; Connectivity; Skill. Headline benefit value: Total outlay Rs 24,104 crore (Centre Rs 15,336 crore + States Rs 8,768 crore) - the largest ever scheme for PVTGs. About 4.9 lakh pucca houses at about Rs 2.39 lakh per house; 500 hostels at about Rs 2.75 crore each; 2,500 anganwadi centres; 3,000 mobile towers; 8,000 km of roads; multi-purpose centres; 1,000 mobile medical units and solar power to 1.5 lakh households. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored with State share; convergence with existing ministries' budgets (DAPST). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 75 PVTGs in about 18 States/UTs and 4.9 lakh PVTG households targeted for saturation. How to apply: Beneficiary identification through baseline surveys by States/UTs; works executed by line departments; no individual application in most components via https://tribal.nic.in (PM-JANMAN dashboard). Documents needed: Household survey/baseline listing as PVTG; Aadhaar; bank account; for housing - land documents as applicable. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Tribal Affairs PM-JANMAN cell; State Tribal Development Departments. Key features: Largest-ever outlay for particularly vulnerable tribal groups; saturation approach (no household left out); 11 interventions across 9 ministries; monitored on the PM Gati Shakti portal Recent updates: Launched November 2023; first villages saturated in 2024-25 with housing, water and road assets; allocation for multi-purpose centres doubled from Rs 150 crore to Rs 300 crore in Budget 2025-26 Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs - PM-JANMAN | https://tribal.nic.in | PIB releases on PM-JANMAN launch and progress | https://www.pib.gov.in.

title: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (nodal; 17 line ministries implementing)
text: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (also known as DAJGUA; other names: Dharti Aaba scheme; Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan; tribal villages saturation mission) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (tribal-majority villages in 30 States/UTs). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (nodal; 17 line ministries implementing). Implementing agency: 17 Central Ministries/Departments with State Governments and district administrations. Scheme type: Mission with convergence funding (Development Action Plan for Scheduled Tribes - DAPST). Launched: 2 October 2024 (launched from Hazaribagh, Jharkhand). Operational period: 2024-25 to 2028-29 (5 years). Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Learned from PM-JANMAN (2023) and subsumed/expanded Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana. Target group: Tribal-majority villages and aspirational blocks - about 5 crore tribal people. Beneficiary type: Village; Family; Community. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: Not applicable (village-based saturation approach). Eligibility: Villages with more than 50% ST population and population above 500, plus aspirational blocks; 63,843 villages in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks across 30 States/UTs Not eligible / conditions: Not an individual application scheme - interventions are planned village-wise by States/line ministries Benefits: Saturation of critical gaps in social infrastructure, health, education, livelihood and connectivity through 25 interventions, including all-weather roads, mobile connectivity, tribal hostels, multipurpose marketing centres, tourist home-stays, FRA patta holder support, sickle-cell disease centres of competence and mobile medical units Benefit type: Infrastructure; Livelihood; Education; Health; Connectivity; Skill. Headline benefit value: Total outlay Rs 79,156 crore over five years (Centre Rs 56,333 crore + States Rs 22,823 crore). Includes 100 tribal multipurpose marketing centres, 25 focus interventions, support for FRA patta holders in agriculture/animal husbandry/fisheries. Funding pattern: Convergence of DAPST funds of 17 ministries with States' own resources. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: 63,843 villages, 549 districts, 2,911 blocks, about 5 crore tribal people across 30 States/UTs. How to apply: Village-level planning by line ministries/States; monitored on the PM Gati Shakti portal with district awards for performance via https://tribal.nic.in/dajgua.aspx. Documents needed: Village plans; beneficiary lists as per component (Aadhaar, bank account, FRA patta etc.). Helpline/contact: Ministry of Tribal Affairs DAJGUA cell (dajgua@tribal.gov.in); District Tribal Welfare Officers. Key features: Largest tribal development mission by outlay; 25 interventions through 17 ministries; saturation approach for tribal-majority villages; builds on PM-JANMAN experience; district-level performance awards Recent updates: Launched 2 October 2024; Budget 2025-26 allocation for DAJGUA quadrupled from Rs 500 crore to Rs 2,000 crore; PMAAGY subsumed under DAJGUA; first progress review in 2025-26 Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs - DAJGUA | https://tribal.nic.in/dajgua.aspx | PIB Lokmattimes/Budget 2025-26 reporting on DAJGUA outlay | https://www.pib.gov.in.

title: Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAAGY)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana (also known as PMAAGY; other names: PM Adi Adarsh Gram; tribal model village scheme) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (tribal villages). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: State Governments/UTs and Gram Panchayats. Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: 2021-22 (with a revised framework issued in 2023). Operational period: 2021-22 onwards; expanded and subsumed into DAJGUA from 2024-25. Current status: Active (subsumed under DAJGUA). Now continued/renamed as: DAJGUA (expanded scope from October 2024). Target group: Tribal villages with more than 50% ST population, including PVTG-majority villages. Beneficiary type: Village. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: Not applicable. Eligibility: Villages with more than 50% ST population; interventions in 9 sectors through 25 components; villages prioritised by tribal population and gaps Not eligible / conditions: Listed-component funding must remain within approved village plans Benefits: Gap-filling support to turn tribal-majority villages into model villages - roads, water, education, health, nutrition, sanitation, livelihood, electrification and digital access Benefit type: Infrastructure; Livelihood; Health; Education. Headline benefit value: Component-wise grants per village as per approved plans (village-level outlays vary); the expanded framework under DAJGUA carries a five-year outlay of about Rs 80,000 crore for the combined mission. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored with State share through DAPST convergence. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of tribal-majority villages identified across 30 States/UTs. How to apply: Through State Tribal Development Departments; village plans and gap assessments via https://tribal.nic.in. Documents needed: Village plan; ST population data; Gram Sabha resolution; utilisation certificates. Helpline/contact: Ministry of Tribal Affairs; State Tribal Welfare Departments. Key features: Predecessor of the DAJGUA saturation model; based on Census/village-level ST concentration; supports PVTG villages on priority Recent updates: Expanded and subsumed under DAJGUA in October 2024 with the outlay rising to about Rs 80,000 crore over five years Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs - PMAAGY | https://tribal.nic.in | Union Budget 2025-26 analysis of tribal welfare allocations | https://www.pib.gov.in.

title: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP) (PMJVM)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (implemented through TRIFED)
text: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP) (also known as PMJVM; other names: Van Dhan Yojana; PMVDY; MSP for minor forest produce; TRIFED tribal livelihood) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (implemented through TRIFED). Implementing agency: Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED) and State agencies/State tribal development corporations. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (100% central funding). Launched: PMVDY launched 14 April 2018; MSP for MFP operational from 2013-14; both consolidated into PMJVM from 2021-22. Operational period: 2018-19 onwards (PMJVM 2021-22 to 2025-26, continuing). Current status: Active. Earlier scheme(s) replaced/merged: Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (2018) and the Scheme of MSP for Minor Forest Produce (2013-14). Target group: Tribal gatherers of minor forest produce (MFP), tribal artisans, tribal entrepreneurs and SHGs. Beneficiary type: Individual; SHG; Entrepreneur. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: No income ceiling; intended for tribal MFP gatherers and artisans. Eligibility: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) are formed as clusters of 15 tribal SHGs with about 300 members each; Value Chain Development Centres process and market MFP; MSP procurement through State agencies Not eligible / conditions: Non-tribal producers are not eligible for MFP MSP support; benefits flow through SHG clusters Benefits: MSP-backed procurement of minor forest produce, value addition and market linkage for tribal products, e-commerce/retail support (Tribes India) and micro-enterprise training for tribal SHG clusters Benefit type: Livelihood; Marketing; MSP support; Skill; Enterprise. Headline benefit value: MSP notified for 50+ MFPs (2021) including tendu, bamboo, honey, lac, gums; VDVKs get working capital of about Rs 15 lakh per cluster; allocation under PMJVM raised to about Rs 380 crore in FY 2025-26 (from about Rs 152 crore). Funding pattern: 100% Central through TRIFED and State agencies. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras established and lakhs of tribal gatherers supported; MFP MSP procurement has moved thousands of crores into tribal households since 2013-14. How to apply: Through State Tribal Development/Cooperation Departments; SHG clusters registered as VDVKs; procurement through designated MSP centres via https://trifed.tribal.gov.in / https://www.trifed.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; SHG membership; bank account; MFP produce records; artisan/vendor registration for Tribes India. Helpline/contact: TRIFED, New Delhi; State Tribal Development Department. Key features: Guarantees a minimum price for forest produce so tribal gatherers do not face distress sales; VDVK cluster model converts SHGs into producer companies; Tribes India retail/e-commerce channel; PMJVM merges MSP and Van Dhan Recent updates: Van Dhan integrated with PMJVM to build tribal producer companies; 50 MFPs covered by MSP; allocation for PMJVM raised to Rs 380.40 crore in FY 2025-26; ongoing tie-ups for tribal product exports Sources: TRIFED - Van Dhan and MSP for MFP | https://trifed.tribal.gov.in | Ministry of Tribal Affairs - PMJVM guidelines | https://tribal.nic.in.

title: Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) Development Plan (PVTG Development Plan)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) Development Plan (also known as PVTG Development Plan; other names: PVTG plan; primitive tribe development scheme) is a PVTG welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (18 States/UTs, 75 PVTGs). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: Ministry of Tribal Affairs with States/UTs. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 1975-76 (identification of primitive tribes); PVTG plan formalised in subsequent Five Year Plans. Operational period: 1975 onwards; continues alongside PM-JANMAN. Current status: Active. Now continued/renamed as: Complemented by PM-JANMAN (2023) and DAJGUA (2024). Target group: 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) identified across 18 States/UTs and one UT. Beneficiary type: Community; Family. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: Not applicable. Eligibility: Communities classified as PVTG (previously Primitive Tribal Groups) living in identified habitations; State-verified lists Not eligible / conditions: Interventions must be in the approved State PVTG plan; land and habitat protection compulsory Benefits: Habitat protection, land development, housing, drinking water, education support, health care and livelihood support for the most vulnerable tribal communities Benefit type: Livelihood; Housing; Health; Education; Habitat protection. Headline benefit value: Central assistance to States for PVTG-focused activities (roughly Rs 25-30 crore per annum range as a centrally sponsored component) plus the much larger PM-JANMAN outlay of Rs 24,104 crore. Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - Central assistance with State complementarity; 100% central for some components. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 75 PVTGs across 18 States/UTs with a population of roughly 40 lakh. How to apply: State Annual Action Plans; household-level benefit lists maintained by State Tribal Departments via https://tribal.nic.in. Documents needed: PVTG household verification; State-approved beneficiary lists; Aadhaar; bank account. Helpline/contact: State Tribal Development Department; Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Key features: Oldest dedicated PVTG support framework predating PM-JANMAN; focus on habitat and traditional rights; now delivered alongside PM-JANMAN's saturation targets Recent updates: Continued in parallel with PM-JANMAN in 2024-26 for activities not covered by saturation interventions; States now report against both frameworks Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs - PVTG development | https://tribal.nic.in | PIB background on PVTG welfare interventions.

title: NSTFDC schemes - Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana, term loans and Adivasi Shiksha Rinn Yojana (NSTFDC)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: NSTFDC schemes - Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana, term loans and Adivasi Shiksha Rinn Yojana (also known as NSTFDC; other names: Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana; AMSY; ST corporation loan) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (through State Channelizing Agencies). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) through State Channelizing Agencies, banks and SHGs. Scheme type: Corporation credit scheme (Government of India company under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs). Launched: NSTFDC incorporated 2001 (under the Companies Act; earlier operations from 1993 as a division). Operational period: 2001 onwards. Current status: Active. Target group: ST individuals, ST women (AMSY), ST SHGs/cooperatives and ST students (education loan). Beneficiary type: Individual; Woman; SHG; Student; Entrepreneur. Age criteria: 18 to 55 years for term loans; not applicable for education loans. Income limit: Annual family income up to Rs 3 lakh (per NSTFDC norms for term loans; verify the current limit). Eligibility: ST individual/SHG with a viable income-generating scheme; ST women for AMSY; ST students with confirmed admission for the education loan; routed through State Channelizing Agencies Not eligible / conditions: Defaulters and non-ST applicants; activity must be permissible and asset-creating Benefits: Concessional term loans (up to 90% of unit cost) for income generation, with an exclusive women's window (AMSY) and education loans for ST students Benefit type: Loan; Micro-credit; Education loan; Livelihood; Women empowerment. Headline benefit value: AMSY: unit cost up to Rs 2 lakh per unit with up to 90% as term loan; interest 4% per annum for beneficiaries (2% for State Channelizing Agencies); repayment up to 5 years. General term loan up to Rs 10 lakh (interest about 6% per annum); ST SHG schemes; education loan limits as per norms. Funding pattern: NSTFDC equity from Government of India; refinance routed through State Channelizing Agencies. Interest rate: About 4% per annum for women under AMSY and about 6% per annum for general term loans. Repayment: Term loans: quarterly instalments over 5 years including moratorium. Education loans: after course completion/employment as per norms. Scale/coverage reported by government: Lakhs of ST beneficiaries financed; AMSY is the largest single ST micro-credit window. How to apply: Through State Channelizing Agencies (State tribal development corporations) with application forms on the NSTFDC website via https://nstfdc.tribal.gov.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; income certificate (up to Rs 3 lakh); Aadhaar; bank account; project estimate/quotation; SHG members list for group loans; for education loan - admission letter and fee details. Helpline/contact: NSTFDC head office, New Delhi; State Channelizing Agency helplines. Key features: Apex ST credit institution; AMSY gives ST women credit at 4% - one of the cheapest loan windows in India; no promoter contribution insisted for AMSY; works only through State channel agencies Recent updates: Digital application tracking introduced; convergence with Van Dhan producer companies and PM-JANMAN livelihood components in 2024-26 Sources: NSTFDC official site | https://nstfdc.tribal.gov.in | State SC/ST development corporation scheme listings (e.g. Kerala KSDCSCST) | https://ksdcscst.com/nstfdc-schemes/.

title: Vocational Training Centres in Tribal Areas / Skill Development for STs (VTC in Tribal Areas)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
text: Vocational Training Centres in Tribal Areas / Skill Development for STs (also known as VTC in Tribal Areas; other names: tribal vocational training centres; skill development tribal youth) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Implementing agency: States/UTs, NGOs and empanelled training institutions. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: Long-running scheme; revised grant norms in the 2010s and 2020s. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Now continued/renamed as: Complemented by PM-DAKSH and DAJGUA skill interventions. Target group: ST youth, especially school dropouts and those in remote areas. Beneficiary type: Individual; Youth; Institution. Age criteria: Youth eligible for vocational courses (generally 18-35 years, as per course norms). Income limit: No strict income ceiling (targeted at tribal youth). Eligibility: ST youth enrolled in short-term vocational courses in trades with market demand; training institutions receive central grants per trainee Not eligible / conditions: Non-tribal youth; courses without placement/market linkage are discouraged Benefits: Free short-term vocational training in trades like computers, tailoring, carpentry, driving, welding, beauty services etc., with stipend, toolkits and placement assistance Benefit type: Skill; Employment; Livelihood. Headline benefit value: Central grant per trainee for training (roughly Rs 15,000-25,000 per trainee per course) plus stipend and toolkit assistance; thousands of trainees per year across States. Funding pattern: 100% Central (grant to States/institutions/voluntary organisations). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of ST youth trained annually; VTCs operate in tribal districts across States. How to apply: Applications through State Tribal Welfare Departments/VTCs; trainee selection by local committees via https://tribal.nic.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; age proof; education certificate; Aadhaar; bank account; photograph. Helpline/contact: State Tribal Welfare Department; Ministry of Tribal Affairs. text: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme (also known as FRA / Forest Rights Act; other names: Forest Rights Act; FRA patta; tribal land rights scheme) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (policy) with Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and States. Implementing agency: State Governments, Forest Rights Committees (village/block/district level), Revenue and Forest Departments. Scheme type: Statutory framework with central support for implementation. Launched: Act passed 2006; came into force 31 December 2007; rules amended 2012. Operational period: 2008 onwards. Current status: Active. Target group: Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. Beneficiary type: Individual; Family; Community. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: No income ceiling. Eligibility: Forest dwellers who have lived in forests for at least three generations (75 years) and depend on forests for livelihood; individual rights (homestead, cultivation) and community rights (community forest resource, grazing, minor forest produce, conversion of pattas) Not eligible / conditions: Claims must be supported by evidence and recommended by the Gram Sabha and Forest Rights Committee; unsupported claims rejected Benefits: Legal recognition of individual and community forest rights including land titles (pattas), rights over minor forest produce, community forest resource management and rehabilitation in case of displacement Benefit type: Land rights; Livelihood; Community rights; Legal. Headline benefit value: Rights-based (no cash grant). About 24-25 lakh individual titles and over 1 lakh community titles recognised since 2008; title holders can access DAJGUA support for agriculture, animal husbandry and fishery under FRA pattas. Funding pattern: Central support for implementation and digitisation; State Governments execute the process. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 25 lakh titles distributed cumulatively; digitisation of claims and records ongoing. How to apply: Claim filed with the Gram Sabha/Forest Rights Committee; verification at block and district level; titles issued by the district administration via https://tribal.nic.in (FRA dashboard) / State FRA portals. Documents needed: Proof of residence and dependency on forest; Gram Sabha resolution; village records; Aadhaar. Helpline/contact: State Tribal Development Department / District FRA cell. Key features: Legal right (not a benefit scheme); Gram Sabha is the primary authority; community forest resource rights allow villages to protect and manage forests; digitisation and FRA cells being funded under DAJGUA Recent updates: DAJGUA includes digitisation and support to FRA claim processes, FRA cells and community forest resource management plans (2024-29); Forest Rights Act claims accelerated in 2024-26 with district-level monitoring Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs - Forest Rights Act | https://tribal.nic.in | DAJGUA intervention list (FRA digitisation and CFR plans) | https://tribal.nic.in/dajgua.aspx.

Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of ashram schools across tribal sub-plan States, educating lakhs of ST students. Eligibility: ST students from rural and remote areas pursuing education; hostels constructed by State Governments, universities or voluntary organisations with central assistance Not eligible / conditions: Only ST students; seats allotted as per State rules Benefits: Construction and maintenance of hostels with mess, study rooms and common facilities so that ST students, particularly girls, can pursue education Benefit type: Hostel; Education; Infrastructure. text: Special Central Assistance to Tribal Sub-Plan / Tribal Sub-Plan strategy (legacy) (also known as SCA to TSP / TSP; other names: Tribal Sub Plan; SCA TSP; TSP strategy) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Tribal Affairs (TSP strategy); Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment handled parts historically. Implementing agency: State Governments/UTs and Integrated Tribal Development Agencies (ITDAs). Scheme type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme / budgetary strategy. Launched: TSP strategy from the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-75); SCA to TSP from 1974-75 onwards. Operational period: 1974-75 to the 2010s-2020s as the main ST funding strategy; now largely integrated into DAPST. Current status: Closed / renamed into DAPST-based planning. Now continued/renamed as: Development Action Plan for Scheduled Tribes (DAPST) based planning and PM-JANMAN/DAJGUA saturation missions. Target group: Scheduled Tribe families and Scheduled Areas (ITDP areas). Beneficiary type: Family; Village; Community. Age criteria: Not applicable. Income limit: ST families, largely below the poverty line, for income-generating support. Eligibility: States with Tribal Sub-Plan areas (ITDPs/MADA clusters/PTG areas) received 100% central grants for income generating schemes, skill development and infrastructure in tribal villages Not eligible / conditions: Funds had to be used in TSP areas only; diversion to non-tribal areas was prohibited Benefits: Income-generating assets, agricultural and horticultural support, minor irrigation, animal husbandry, education and infrastructure in tribal sub-plan areas, implemented through ITDAs Benefit type: Livelihood; Infrastructure; Skill. Headline benefit value: 100% central assistance allocated to States in proportion to ST population; grants per family/unit as per State schemes; funded thousands of village-level assets over five decades. Funding pattern: 100% central assistance to States (Centrally Sponsored Scheme). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Operated across all TSP States, covering millions of ST beneficiaries over five decades. How to apply: Through State tribal departments/ITDAs with beneficiary selection by local committees (historical scheme) via Not applicable (historical) - see https://tribal.nic.in. Documents needed: ST certificate; BPL/income proof; Aadhaar; land records where applicable (historical). Helpline/contact: State Integrated Tribal Development Agency (ITDA). Key features: The backbone of tribal development finance in India for nearly 50 years; ITDA-based delivery in Scheduled Areas; replaced by outcome-oriented DAPST and saturation missions after 2018 Recent updates: SCA to TSP as a standalone fund has largely given way to DAPST earmarking (2018-19 onwards) and now PM-JANMAN (2023) and DAJGUA (2024) - include as a historical scheme in time-series answers Sources: Ministry of Tribal Affairs - Tribal Sub Plan background | https://tribal.nic.in | CAG/Standing Committee reports on SCA to TSP utilisation.

title: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub (NSSH / SC-ST Hub)
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
text: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub (also known as NSSH / SC-ST Hub; other names: SC ST Hub; National SC ST Hub; MSME SC ST hub scheme) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. Implementing agency: National SC-ST Hub office; NSIC, SIDBI, NABARD, industry associations, IITs/management institutes. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 2016 (launched by the Prime Minister in October 2016; extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26). Operational period: FY 2017-18 to FY 2025-26 (extensions being processed). Current status: Active. Target group: SC/ST owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and SC/ST entrepreneurs. Beneficiary type: Entrepreneur; MSME. Age criteria: 18 years and above. Income limit: No income ceiling (enterprise-based scheme). Eligibility: MSME with Udyam Registration (or willing to register) having at least 51% SC/ST ownership; manufacturing, service, trading or agri-allied enterprise for most components; for SCLCSS - SC/ST ownership above 51% with institutional loan for new plant and machinery Not eligible / conditions: Non-SC/ST majority enterprises; second-hand machinery (for capital subsidy); dual benefit from a similar subsidy is not allowed Benefits: Capacity building and training, Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy (SCLCSS), procurement support to meet the 4% government procurement mandate, GeM and Single Point Registration assistance, reimbursement of bank loan processing fees, exhibition/marketing support and mentorship Benefit type: Subsidy; Training; Marketing; Procurement support; Credit facilitation. Headline benefit value: Capital subsidy of 25% on institutional loan for plant and machinery, capped at Rs 25 lakh (SCLCSS); up to 90% of course fee capped at Rs 1 lakh for training reimbursements; up to 80% of pledge/bank-guarantee charges capped at Rs 1 lakh for tender participation; 100% subsidy on NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme fees. Funding pattern: 100% Central (outlay about Rs 588 crore for 2021-22 to 2025-26). Interest rate: Not applicable (interest is as per the lending bank's rate; subsidy reduces capital cost). Repayment: As per the institutional loan (term loan repayment over 5-7 years typically). Scale/coverage reported by government: Over 1 lakh SC/ST MSEs supported through training, subsidy and procurement handholding since 2016; government procurement from SC/ST MSEs is tracked against the 4% mandate under the Public Procurement Policy. How to apply: Online registration on the SC-ST Hub portal; SCLCSS applications routed offline through the prime lending institution (bank) to SIDBI/NABARD via https://www.scsthub.in. Documents needed: Udyam Registration certificate; SC/ST caste certificate of proprietor/directors; ownership proof showing 51%+ SC/ST shareholding; PAN; GST; project report; machinery quotations/invoices for SCLCSS; loan sanction letter; bank account. Helpline/contact: SC-ST Hub helpline (Ministry of MSME); offices in major cities including Delhi. Key features: One-stop support system for SC/ST entrepreneurs; addresses the 4% public procurement mandate; includes the biggest SC/ST capital subsidy (25%, up to Rs 25 lakh); training and market access through NSIC/GeM Recent updates: Scheme extended to 2025-26 with about Rs 588 crore outlay; GeM/NSIC onboarding and vendor-development programmes expanded in 2024-26; SCLCSS disbursals tracked on the MSME MIS portal Sources: National SC-ST Hub portal | https://www.scsthub.in | Ministry of MSME - NSSH guidelines and scheme details | https://msme.gov.in.

title: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS)
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (sub-scheme under National SC-ST Hub)
text: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (also known as SCLCSS; other names: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy; SC ST capital subsidy 25%) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (sub-scheme under National SC-ST Hub). Implementing agency: Prime Lending Institutions (banks) with nodal agencies SIDBI and NABARD; subsidy released through PFMS. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (sub-scheme of NSSH). Launched: 2016 (sub-scheme of the National SC-ST Hub). Operational period: FY 2017-18 to FY 2025-26. Current status: Active. Target group: SC/ST owned micro and small enterprises (manufacturing and services). Beneficiary type: MSME; Entrepreneur. Age criteria: 18 years and above (proprietor/directors). Income limit: No income ceiling. Eligibility: Micro or small enterprise with valid Udyam Registration and at least 51% SC/ST ownership; institutional term loan sanctioned for purchase of new plant and machinery/equipment; no sector-specific restriction; SC/ST units upgraded to medium within 3 years remain eligible Not eligible / conditions: Second-hand machinery; enterprises without institutional finance; applicants who already got a similar capital subsidy (no dual benefit) Benefits: Capital subsidy to reduce the cost of new plant and machinery financed by a bank/institution, improving the viability of SC/ST manufacturing and service units Benefit type: Subsidy; Capital investment support. Headline benefit value: 25% capital subsidy on the institutional loan amount, capped at Rs 25,00,000 per enterprise (eligible term loan typically up to Rs 1 crore). Funding pattern: 100% Central; disbursed through SIDBI/NABARD to the lending bank account of the beneficiary. Interest rate: Not applicable (bank interest applies; subsidy reduces effective cost). Repayment: As per the underlying term loan (usually 5 to 7 years). Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of SC/ST MSEs given capital subsidy for modernisation since 2017-18. How to apply: Offline: obtain bank term loan, then the bank forwards the subsidy application to the nodal agency (SIDBI/NABARD) on the MSME MIS portal via https://www.scsthub.in (SCLCSS) / MSME MIS portal. Documents needed: Udyam Registration; PAN; SC/ST caste certificate of all partners/directors; partnership deed or MOA/AOA; proof of 51%+ SC/ST shareholding; machinery/equipment invoices and payment receipts; bank sanction letter. Helpline/contact: SC-ST Hub helpline; MSME Development Institutes (MSME-DIs). Key features: Highest-value capital subsidy available to SC/ST MSMEs; works only with bank finance (not on cash purchases); applies to manufacturing and service machinery/technology upgradation Recent updates: Subsidy claims continue under NSSH till 2025-26; MSME Ministry has pushed awareness campaigns through MSME-DIs and state SC/ST corporations in 2024-26 Sources: National SC-ST Hub - SCLCSS | https://www.scsthub.in | Ministry of MSME | https://msme.gov.in.

title: Stand-Up India Scheme (SUI)
ministry: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
text: Stand-Up India Scheme (also known as SUI; other names: Stand Up India loan; SC ST woman entrepreneur loan 10 lakh to 1 crore) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. Implementing agency: All scheduled commercial banks (public and private) - over 1.25 lakh branches; SIDBI operates the Standup Mitra handholding portal. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (credit guarantee backed). Launched: 5 April 2016. Operational period: 2016 onwards. Current status: Active. Target group: SC, ST and women entrepreneurs setting up greenfield enterprises. Beneficiary type: Entrepreneur. Age criteria: 18 years and above. Income limit: No income ceiling. Eligibility: SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneur; greenfield project (first venture of the beneficiary in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activity); for non-individual entities at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake must be with SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneurs; borrower must not be a defaulter to any bank/financial institution Not eligible / conditions: Expansion of existing business; retail trading restricted in certain years; persons with existing bank defaults Benefits: Composite bank loan (term loan plus working capital) for new enterprises, with collateral-free credit up to Rs 1 crore covered under the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Stand-Up India Loans, plus Rupay debit card and handholding support through the Standup Mitra portal Benefit type: Loan; Credit guarantee; Entrepreneurship. Headline benefit value: Composite loan of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore per borrower (loan limit raised/announced to Rs 2 crore under the 2025 relaunch for eligible categories - confirm with the bank). Margin money 25% of project cost, of which at least 10% must come from the borrower; the rest can come from convergence with other schemes. Funding pattern: Bank credit with credit guarantee support from the Government of India (CGTMSE/NCGTC). Interest rate: Bank rate linked to MCLR/repo - normally the lowest applicable rate for that loan category; no collateral required up to Rs 1 crore. Repayment: Up to 7 years with a moratorium of up to 18 months. Scale/coverage reported by government: Over 2.5 lakh loans target across bank branches; each branch is expected to finance at least one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur. How to apply: Apply at any scheduled commercial bank branch or online through the Standup Mitra portal; SIDBI provides handholding via https://www.standupmitra.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate (for SC/ST), identity and address proof, PAN, Aadhaar, business plan/project report, quotation for machinery, bank statements, proof of business premises. Helpline/contact: Standup Mitra helpline (SIDBI); bank branch managers. text: PM-DAKSH - Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi Yojana (also known as PM-DAKSH; other names: PM Daksh skill scheme; skill development SC OBC DNT sanitation workers) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Implementing agency: National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), MSDE agencies, Sector Skill Councils, empanelled training partners and state corporations. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 2020 (announced 2020-21; expanded 2021-22 onwards). Operational period: 2020-21 to 2025-26. Current status: Active. Target group: SC, OBC, DNT, EBC, sanitation workers and waste pickers (18-45 years). Beneficiary type: Individual; Youth. Age criteria: 18 to 45 years. Income limit: Target-group based eligibility (no separate income ceiling in the main guidelines). Eligibility: Persons from SC/OBC/DNT/EBC/sanitation-worker families seeking wage or self-employment; selection through empanelled training partners; courses of 3 weeks (short-term), 3-6 months (upgradation) and 1 year (long-term/entrepreneurship) Not eligible / conditions: Persons who have already received similar skill training under another government scheme in the same trade; beneficiaries must complete assessment Benefits: Free skill training with stipend, toolkits, certification and placement/self-employment support; covers wage employment, self-employment, entrepreneurship and upskilling for existing artisans Benefit type: Skill; Employment; Stipend; Toolkits. Headline benefit value: Fully funded training (about Rs 10,000-30,000 per trainee depending on course duration) plus stipend of about Rs 500-1,500 per month, toolkits worth up to Rs 5,000-15,000 and assessment/certification charges; allocation increased from about Rs 92 crore to Rs 130 crore in recent budgets. Funding pattern: 100% Central. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Lakhs of candidates trained since 2020-21 across SC/OBC/DNT/EBC/sanitation-worker categories. How to apply: Online registration on the PM-DAKSH portal; allotment to an empanelled training partner via https://pmdaksh.dosje.gov.in. Key features: Covers SC, OBC, DNT, EBC and sanitation workers in a single skilling window; stipend and toolkit to make training attractive; placement tracking through NSDC; long-term courses for school dropouts Recent updates: Budget allocation raised from about Rs 92.47 crore to about Rs 130 crore; strong emphasis on placement-linked courses in 2024-26; convergence with NAMASTE for sanitation workers' upskilling Sources: PM-DAKSH portal | https://pmdaksh.dosje.gov.in | Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment | https://socialjustice.gov.in.

title: National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (NSCEM)
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (with Ministry of Tribal Affairs for tribal outreach)
text: National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (also known as NSCEM; other names: Sickle cell mission 2047; sickle cell anaemia elimination programme) is a ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: 278 districts in 17 States (tribal high-prevalence areas). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (with Ministry of Tribal Affairs for tribal outreach). Implementing agency: States/UTs under the National Health Mission; health departments and medical colleges. Scheme type: National Mission (Centrally Sponsored through National Health Mission). Launched: Announced in Union Budget 2023-24; launched on 1 July 2023. Operational period: 2023 to 2047 (target year for elimination). Current status: Active. Target group: Tribal population and others in high-prevalence districts - screening for the 0-40 age group. Beneficiary type: Individual; Family; Community. Age criteria: Universal screening for the 0-40 years population in identified districts. Income limit: No income ceiling. Eligibility: Residents of the 278 identified districts in 17 States with high sickle cell disease prevalence; screening, counselling and treatment free of cost Not eligible / conditions: Not a cash-benefit scheme; services are health interventions Benefits: Free screening (HbS test) for sickle cell status, colour-coded cards, pre-marital and prenatal counselling, treatment and management support, and dedicated centres of competence Benefit type: Health; Screening; Treatment; Awareness. Headline benefit value: About 7 crore people to be screened (0-40 years) in 278 districts; over 1 crore people screened within the first year; budget through NHM with 60:40 Centre:State sharing; DAJGUA funds sickle-cell centres of competence and counselling support. Funding pattern: National Health Mission - 60:40 Centre:State (90:10 for NE/Himalayan States). Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: About 7 crore people targeted for screening; 278 districts, 17 States (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, WB, TN, Telangana, AP, Karnataka, Assam, UP, Kerala, Bihar, Uttarakhand). How to apply: No application - screening through health camps, anganwadi and school-based drives, and health facilities via https://sicklecell.nhm.gov.in (National Sickle Cell Portal). Documents needed: Aadhaar/identity proof for registration at screening camps; existing health records if any. Helpline/contact: National Health Mission health helpline (104/1075 in many States). Key features: Mission-mode elimination of sickle cell disease by 2047; about 1 in 86 tribal births affected; colour-coded cards for diseased/carrier/normal status; part of the tribal health agenda with DAJGUA support Recent updates: More than 1 crore people screened by 2024; centres of competence and counselling support funded under DAJGUA (2024-29); expansion of screening to all tribal habitations Sources: National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (MoHFW/NHM) | https://sicklecell.nhm.gov.in | PIB/DD News updates on sickle cell screening progress | https://www.pib.gov.in.

text: UGC Post-Doctoral Fellowship for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Candidates (also known as UGC PDF (SC/ST); other names: post doctoral fellowship SC ST; UGC PDF SC ST amount) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. Implementing agency: University Grants Commission directly to fellows through universities/colleges. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: Running since the 1990s-2000s; award rates revised with effect from 1 December 2014 (and later). Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Eligibility: PhD degree in any subject; at least 50% marks at graduation and 55% at post-graduation; research to be conducted at a UGC-recognised university/college/institute of national importance; NOC from the proposed research centre needed Not eligible / conditions: Candidates already in employment or receiving another fellowship must resign before joining; fellowship terminates on resignation; no extension beyond the sanctioned duration Benefits: Monthly post-doctoral fellowship for 5 years, contingency grant for research expenses, HRA as per institution rules and escort/reader assistance for persons with disabilities - all through DBT Benefit type: Fellowship; Research; Education. Headline benefit value: Rs 38,800 per month for the first two years and Rs 46,500 per month from the third year; contingency grant Rs 50,000 per year; escort/reader assistance Rs 2,000 per month for PwD candidates; duration 5 years with no extension. ministry: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education)
text: Tuition fee waiver, free messing and pocket allowance for SC/ST/PwD students in IITs, NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutions (also known as CFTI fee waiver (SC/ST); other names: IIT SC ST fee waiver; NIT free messing SC ST; tuition waiver SC ST IIT) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India (all IITs, NITs, IIITs, IIESTs and other centrally funded technical institutions). Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education). Implementing agency: Individual IITs, NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded institutions. Scheme type: Institution-level fee waiver mandated by the Ministry of Education. Launched: 2005-06 (fee waiver) with enhanced benefits from 2016 and extended for 2021-26, continuing. Operational period: Continuous. Current status: Active. Target group: SC, ST and PwD students (UG and PG) admitted to centrally funded technical institutions. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines. Income limit: Tuition waiver is available to all SC/ST/PwD students; free messing, hostel rent exemption and pocket allowance are means-linked (commonly family income up to Rs 5 lakh; some institutes extend support up to Rs 8 lakh). Eligibility: Admission through JoSAA/JEE or the institute's own admission process; caste/disability certificate submitted to the institute's academic/financial aid office; registration and academic progress norms apply Not eligible / conditions: Waiver does not cover hostel/mess charges beyond the scheme design in all institutes; benefits are for the standard duration of the programme; lapses if the student drops out or fails to maintain registration Benefits: Full tuition fee exemption for SC/ST/PwD students, plus (for means-qualifying students) free basic messing, hostel room-rent exemption and a monthly pocket allowance - making premier technical education nearly free for SC/ST students Benefit type: Fee waiver; Stipend; Hostel; Education. Headline benefit value: Full tuition waiver (worth about Rs 8-10 lakh over a 4-year B.Tech); free basic messing (worth about Rs 40,000-60,000 per year at most institutes); hostel rent exemption; pocket allowance of about Rs 250-500 per month, and up to about Rs 1,000 per month at some institutes such as IIT Delhi for income up to Rs 8 lakh. Funding pattern: 100% Central through the institutions' internal fee waiver and financial aid budgets. Interest rate: Not applicable. Repayment: Not applicable. Scale/coverage reported by government: Thousands of SC/ST students in every admission batch across the 23 IITs, 31 NITs, 25+ IIITs and other CFTIs. How to apply: Automatic on admission - student submits the caste certificate and income certificate at reporting/financial-aid office; no separate online scheme application via Individual institute academic/financial-aid portals (e.g. https://academic.iitd.ac.in). Documents needed: SC/ST/PwD caste or disability certificate; income certificate (for means-linked benefits); admission/registration proof; bank account; Aadhaar. Helpline/contact: Academic/Financial Aid Office of the concerned institution. Key features: Not a classic 'apply-online' scheme - it is an automatic statutory benefit at CFTIs; free messing plus pocket allowance makes hostel life affordable; income-linked benefits for SC/ST up to Rs 5-8 lakh; very few eligible students claim it Recent updates: Better-off families (income above Rs 5 lakh) pay a higher tuition slab in some institutions; SC/ST/PwD waiver continues; institutes have been asked to publicise the waiver to increase uptake among SC/ST students Sources: IIT Bombay fee waiver and free messing notification | https://www.iitb.ac.in/newacadhome/M.Sc.FM2019.pdf | Ministry of Education norms on SC/ST/PwD tuition fee waiver in CFTIs | https://www.education.gov.in.

title: PM Vidyalaxmi (education loan with collateral-free guarantee) (PM Vidyalaxmi)
ministry: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education)
text: PM Vidyalaxmi (education loan with collateral-free guarantee) (also known as PM Vidyalaxmi; other names: PM Vidyalaxmi scheme education loan; collateral free loan students 2024) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the central level. State/UT coverage: All India. Nodal ministry/department: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education). Implementing agency: Banks/financial institutions with the Credit Guarantee Fund for Education Loans (CGFSEL) and the Vidya Lakshmi portal. Scheme type: Central Sector Scheme (credit guarantee + interest subvention). Launched: Announced in Union Budget 2024-25; guidelines notified in November 2024. Operational period: 2024-25 onwards. Current status: Active. Target group: Students admitted to higher education institutions ranked in the top 860 NIRF institutions, including SC/ST students from low-income families. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: As per bank norms. Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 8,00,000 (for the collateral-free guarantee and 3% interest subvention components). Eligibility: Admission to a recognised institution (as notified); loan through the Vidya Lakshmi portal; for collateral-free loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh, the guarantee is provided under CGFSEL; for loans up to Rs 10 lakh with full collateral-free cover under specific conditions; interest subvention for income up to Rs 4.5 lakh during the moratorium Not eligible / conditions: Institutions/students outside the notified list; benefit cannot be combined with certain other loan-linked subsidies Benefits: Collateral-free education loan with a Government guarantee, plus interest subvention during the study/moratorium period for low-income families - removing the need for family assets as security Benefit type: Education loan; Credit guarantee; Interest subvention. Headline benefit value: Collateral-free education loans with 75% guarantee cover by the Government for loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh; 90% cover for top-250 NIRF institutions; 3% interest subvention during moratorium for family income up to Rs 4.5 lakh (Central-sector students). Funding pattern: 100% Central (guarantee fund + subvention). Interest rate: As per the bank's education-loan rate; reduced by 3% subvention during the moratorium for eligible families. Repayment: As per bank education-loan norms (moratorium during course plus typically 1 year, then 10-15 years). Scale/coverage reported by government: About 7 lakh students expected to benefit every year; total outlay of about Rs 3,600 crore for 2024-25 to 2031-32. How to apply: Apply through the Vidya Lakshmi portal (single window for education loans) via https://www.vidyalakshmi.co.in. Documents needed: Admission letter; fee structure; income certificate; caste certificate where applicable; Aadhaar; bank statements; co-borrower/guarantor details as applicable. Helpline/contact: Vidya Lakshmi portal helpdesk; bank education-loan desks. Key features: Removes the collateral requirement that blocked SC/ST students from education loans; launched in 2024 and therefore the newest major student-benefit scheme; complements Post-Matric Scholarships for students above income ceilings Recent updates: Guidelines issued November 2024; banks onboarding through Vidya Lakshmi; expansion of eligible-institution list and awareness drives in 2025-26 Sources: Department of Higher Education / PIB PM Vidyalaxmi guidelines (2024) | https://www.education.gov.in | Vidya Lakshmi portal | https://www.vidyalakshmi.co.in.

text: Karnataka State Scholarship Portal - Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships for SC/ST students (SSP) (also known as Karnataka SSP (SC/ST); other names: Karnataka SSP scholarship; Karnataka post matric SC ST scholarship amount) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the state level. State/UT coverage: Karnataka. Nodal ministry/department: Social Welfare Department and Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka. Implementing agency: Karnataka State Scholarship Portal (SSP) with college, taluk and district verification. Scheme type: State Sector + Centrally Sponsored (state share on top of central scholarships). Launched: Not specified. Operational period: Not specified. Current status: Active. Target group: SC and ST students from Class 1 to post-graduation, including professional courses. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Not specified in the scheme guidelines. Income limit: SC/ST pre-matric Class 9-10 upto Rs 2,50,000 (central norms); Classes 1-8 state-funded with a higher ceiling (about Rs 6 lakh); post-matric up to Rs 2.50 lakh for full benefit, with partial fee waiver for engineering/medical students whose family income is between Rs 2.5 lakh and Rs 10 lakh. Eligibility: Karnataka domicile; Aadhaar-linked bank account; minimum marks (about 50%) and 75% attendance for post-matric benefits; institution must be recognised Not eligible / conditions: Students repeating the same course more than once; not more than two male children per family get post-matric hostel/fee benefits (no limit for girls) Benefits: Fee reimbursement, maintenance allowance and hostel/food support for SC/ST students from school to professional courses, disbursed by DBT through the single-window SSP Benefit type: Scholarship; Fee reimbursement; Hostel; Education. Headline benefit value: Scholarships of about Rs 2,500 to Rs 13,500 per year depending on class/course; full or partial fee waiver (50% waiver for engineering/medical students with family income Rs 2.5-10 lakh); fee reimbursement for SC/ST engineering and medical students whose parents are serving in the armed forces. Funding pattern: State Government budget (State Sector Scheme; some state schemes also carry a central share). How to apply: Online only through the Karnataka State Scholarship Portal (SSP) with Aadhaar e-KYC via https://ssp.postmatric.karnataka.gov.in. Documents needed: Caste certificate; income certificate; Aadhaar-linked bank account; marksheets; admission/bonafide certificate; attendance certificate; domicile. Helpline/contact: Karnataka SSP helpline; district Social Welfare/Tribal Welfare offices. Key features: Single window for all Karnataka scholarships; separate SC and ST departments; partial fee waiver even for higher-income SC/ST professional students; strict attendance and marks conditions for renewal Sources: Karnataka State Scholarship Portal | https://ssp.postmatric.karnataka.gov.in | Karnataka Social Welfare Department scholarship schedules.

text: Telangana Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi (foreign education assistance for SC/ST students) (also known as Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi; other names: Telangana overseas scholarship SC ST; Ambedkar overseas vidya nidhi amount) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the state level. State/UT coverage: Telangana. Nodal ministry/department: Social Welfare Department (SC) and Tribal Welfare Department (ST), Government of Telangana. Implementing agency: Telangana ePASS portal with departmental committees. Scheme type: State Sector Scheme. Launched: Not specified. Operational period: Not specified. Current status: Active. Target group: SC and ST students from Telangana admitted to postgraduate/doctoral courses abroad. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Below 35 years. Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 5,00,000. Eligibility: At least 60% marks in the qualifying degree; admission to a recognised foreign university in notified countries (USA, UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand etc.); minimum GRE/GMAT/IELTS/TOEFL scores; only one student per family Not eligible / conditions: Only one student per family; quota-limited (about 1,900 beneficiaries in the 2025 cycle) and selection is now fully merit-based Benefits: Financial assistance covering tuition, living expenses, visa fees and a one-way economy airfare for SC/ST students going abroad for higher studies Benefit type: Scholarship; Education; Overseas study. Headline benefit value: Up to Rs 20,00,000 per selected student (released in two instalments), plus visa fees and one-way economy airfare; beneficiary quota increased from 1,100 to 1,900 for the 2025 cycle. title: Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme (BSCC)
ministry: Education Department, Government of Bihar (with the Planning and Development Department)
text: Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme (also known as BSCC; other names: Bihar student credit card loan amount; education loan Bihar students) is a SC & ST welfare scheme of the Government of India at the state level. State/UT coverage: Bihar. Nodal ministry/department: Education Department, Government of Bihar (with the Planning and Development Department). Implementing agency: DRCC/district officials with the State's single-window portal. Scheme type: State Sector credit scheme. Launched: 2016-17. Operational period: Not specified. Current status: Active. Target group: Students of Bihar, including SC/ST students, pursuing higher education after Class 12. Beneficiary type: Student. Age criteria: Up to 25 years. Income limit: No family income ceiling for the scheme. Eligibility: Bihar resident; passed Class 12; admission to a recognised higher-education course (general, technical or professional) in Bihar or outside; not a defaulter Not eligible / conditions: Only one loan per student; course must be recognised; repayment responsibility shared between the student and the State Benefits: Education loan on easy terms with the State paying interest during the study period and offering repayment support, so that no student is denied education for want of money Benefit type: Education loan; Education. Headline benefit value: Loan up to Rs 4,00,000 per student for tuition and other expenses; simple interest of about 4% per annum; 50% of the interest paid by the State; if the loan and interest are repaid on time, the State pays half of the principal back; repayment over 7 years after the moratorium. Funding pattern: State Government (interest support and repayment incentive) with bank credit. Interest rate: About 4% per annum simple interest, of which the State pays 50%. Repayment: After course completion plus a moratorium; 7-year repayment window with a State incentive of half the principal on timely repayment. Scale/coverage reported by government: Over 1 lakh students have benefited since 2016-17. How to apply: Online application through the State's Student Credit Card portal, then district-level processing via https://www.7nishchayyuvaup.gov.in / Bihar Student Credit Card portal. Documents needed: Class 12 marksheet; admission letter/fee structure; Aadhaar; residence proof; bank account; caste certificate for SC/ST records; photographs. Helpline/contact: Bihar Student Credit Card helpline; DRCC district offices. Key features: State-backed education loan with interest subsidy and principal repayment incentive; open to all categories with no income ceiling - particularly useful for SC/ST students above scholarship income limits; one of the most successful state education-loan models Sources: Government of Bihar - Student Credit Card Scheme | https://www.7nishchayyuvaup.gov.in.
